rules.what_you_get: A free repair or, if it can't be fixed, a free replacement. Cuisinart calls this its hassle-free replacement warranty and will send you a return shipping label so you are not out of pocket for postage. Coffee grinders are 18 months instead of 3 years, and outdoor grills vary.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the product inquiry form on Cuisinart's site or call their consumer service line to get a free return shipping label. You must have bought it from Cuisinart or an approved seller.
rules.script_hint: My Cuisinart has failed and it's under three years old. Cuisinart's standard warranty is three years with hassle-free replacement, so please send me a return shipping label.

rules.title: Cuisinart pans, knives and tools: covered for your lifetime
rules.window_note: For as long as the person who bought it is alive. There is genuinely no expiry date on this one.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, a free identical or equivalent replacement, or your money back if they cannot do either. This covers Cuisinart cookware, cutlery, and tools and gadgets, but not the electrical appliances, which get 3 years instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Email through the product inquiry form or call to get a free return shipping label. Normal wear and tear is not covered, so describe an actual defect: a handle that snapped off, a pan base that warped or separated, a blade that cracked. Without a receipt they use the date it was made.
rules.script_hint: My Cuisinart cookware has a manufacturing defect. Cuisinart cookware carries a lifetime warranty for the original purchaser, so I'd like it repaired or replaced and a return shipping label sent.

rules.title: KitchenAid tools and gadgets: free for a year, covered for life after
rules.window_note: Year 1 is a straight swap for a new one. Year 2 onwards runs for the life of the product with no end date.
rules.what_you_get: In the first year, a free replacement, no questions about repairing it. From year two onwards, for the life of the product, anything found to be defective gets repaired free or replaced with the same item or something of equal or better value. This covers the KitchenAid hand tools and gadgets range, not the stand mixers or the big appliances.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the KitchenAid customer satisfaction line to start the claim, or post the item to their consumer service department in Trenton, New Jersey. You pay the postage to send it in. Normal use and care is the test, so describe a real defect rather than damage from dropping it.
rules.script_hint: My KitchenAid tool has a defect in materials or workmanship. KitchenAid tools and gadgets carry a lifetime limited warranty from year two onward, so I'd like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: Frigidaire dishwasher: tub covered for life, racks to year 5
rules.window_note: The stainless tub and door liner have no expiry date. The racks and the electronic control module are covered in years 2 through 5. The machine as a whole is 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: A free stainless tub or door liner for as long as you own the dishwasher, and a free set of racks or a free control board up to the end of year 5. The control board is the part that usually kills a dishwasher, so that 5-year cover is worth checking before you replace the machine.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Frigidaire with your model and serial number, on a sticker on the edge of the door. Say which part has failed and which tier of the warranty you are claiming under. These extra tiers are parts only, so budget for the repair person's time.
rules.script_hint: My Frigidaire dishwasher's electronic control module has failed and the machine is under five years old. Frigidaire covers the control module for parts in years two through five, so please supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Frigidaire stacked laundry: tub for life, motor for 10 years
rules.window_note: The inner wash tub has no time limit. The motor runs to 10 years. The unit as a whole is covered for 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: A free inner wash tub with no deadline, and a free motor for ten years, on Frigidaire laundry centers (the stacked washer-and-dryer-in-one units). Standalone Frigidaire washers and dryers only get the 1 year, so this extra cover is specific to the stacked units and easy to miss.
rules.how_to_claim: Confirm you have a laundry center rather than a separate washer and dryer. Call Frigidaire with the model and serial number and name the motor or the inner wash tub specifically. These are parts-only tiers, so you cover the labour.
rules.script_hint: I have a Frigidaire laundry center and the motor has failed. Laundry centers carry a 10-year parts warranty on the motor, so please supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Frigidaire garbage disposal: up to 12 years, plus rust cover for life
rules.window_note: How long depends on the motor size: 12 years for a 1.25 horsepower unit, 10 years for 0.75 horsepower, and 5 or 6 years for a 0.5 horsepower unit. Rusting through has no time limit at all.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement disposal unit for anything from 5 to 12 years depending on which one you bought, plus lifetime cover if it corrodes. People replace jammed or leaking disposals without ever checking, because nobody expects a warranty this long on a part hidden under the sink.
rules.how_to_claim: Look under the sink for the label on the disposal body giving the model and horsepower rating, then match that to the length above. Call Frigidaire and quote the horsepower, since that is what sets your window.
rules.script_hint: My Frigidaire garbage disposal has failed. It's a three-quarter horsepower unit, which carries a 10-year warranty, and mine is inside that window. I'd like a replacement under warranty.

rules.title: "Warranty void if this sticker is broken" is generally not allowed
rules.window_note: Works any time your written warranty is still running.
rules.what_you_get: Opening the case or breaking a seal to do normal maintenance or a repair does not kill your warranty. You still get the repair or replacement you were promised. In July 2024 the FTC sent warning letters to PC and parts makers over exactly these stickers.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask for the warranty repair as normal. If they refuse because a seal was broken, tell them the sticker doesn't cancel your rights and ask them to show what damage you actually caused. If they still refuse, report them to the FTC.
rules.script_hint: The FTC has warned companies that "warranty void if removed" stickers break the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act. Breaking that seal doesn't cancel my warranty. Please book the repair.

rules.title: If it came with any written warranty, the built-in "it should work" promise can't be taken away
rules.window_note: Runs alongside the written warranty. In most states you have about 4 years from the purchase date to make the claim. If the written one is a 'limited' warranty the company may cap this second one to the same length; if it is a 'full' warranty they cannot cap it at all. Then escalate to your state attorney general's consumer protection office.
rules.what_you_get: On top of whatever the paper warranty says, you also have the law's built-in promise that the product actually does what it's supposed to do. If a company gives you a written warranty, it is not allowed to cancel that built-in promise. Same if it sold you a service contract.
rules.how_to_claim: If the written warranty just ran out, or doesn't cover your particular problem, write to the seller and the maker and say you are also claiming the implied warranty of merchantability, which they were never allowed to cancel.
rules.script_hint: You gave a written warranty on this product, so under federal law you can't disclaim the implied warranty that it works. It failed far too soon for a product like this. I'd like it repaired or my money back.

rules.title: A limited warranty can only shorten the built-in promise to its own length, never shorter
rules.window_note: Lasts at least as long as the written warranty. Some states ignore these cut-offs entirely and give you longer.
rules.what_you_get: If your limited warranty runs 2 years, the built-in "it works" promise runs at least 2 years too. A company with a 1-year warranty cannot shrink your built-in promise down to 90 days. And a warranty labelled "Full" can't shorten it at all.
rules.how_to_claim: If they tell you the implied warranty expired earlier than the written warranty, point out that the law only lets them match it to their own warranty length, not cut it shorter.
rules.script_hint: Your written warranty runs [X] years, so the implied warranty runs at least that long as well. Federal law doesn't let you cut it shorter than your own warranty period.

rules.title: You usually have about 4 years from the purchase date to make a warranty claim stick
rules.window_note: About 4 years from the purchase date in most states. This is your deadline to act. It does NOT mean the product has to last 4 years.
rules.what_you_get: Time. Even after the printed warranty has run out, the law's built-in promise can usually still be enforced for roughly 4 years from when you bought it, as long as the fault was already there when it was sold to you.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your receipt and check the date. If it's under about 4 years, write to the seller and the maker and say the fault was built in from the start, so you're still inside the time limit.
rules.script_hint: I bought this on [date], which is inside the time limit for a warranty claim in this state. The fault was there from the start, so please repair, replace or refund it.

rules.title: Massachusetts: "sold as is" doesn't work, and you can ask a court for up to triple your money
rules.window_note: Send the demand letter as soon as you can. You have to wait 30 days after sending it before you can file in court.
rules.what_you_get: In Massachusetts, any wording a seller or maker uses to cancel the built-in promise that a product works is simply void. "As is" and "no warranty" don't count, and they can't be waived by agreement. On top of that, if you send a proper 30-day demand letter and they ignore it or lowball you on purpose, a court can award you two to three times your loss plus your lawyer's fees.
rules.how_to_claim: Write a letter (keep a copy) saying who you are, exactly what went wrong, what it cost you, and what you want them to do. Mail it to the company. Wait 30 days. If they don't make a fair offer, you can file in court and ask for multiplied damages and your legal costs.
rules.script_hint: This is a 30-day demand letter under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 93A. Any "as is" or disclaimer wording is void here under Chapter 106 Section 2-316A. Please repair or refund within 30 days.

rules.title: Maryland: "as is" doesn't hold up, and the maker has to fix things quickly
rules.window_note: Applies to consumer goods and services. Older cars over 6 model years old with more than 60,000 miles are treated differently.
rules.what_you_get: In Maryland, wording a seller uses to cancel or cut back the built-in promise that a product works is unenforceable. And a maker can only limit what you get under its own written warranty if it actually gives you a reasonable and quick way to get the warranty work done. If it doesn't, those limits don't hold either.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller that Maryland law makes "as is" and disclaimer wording unenforceable on consumer goods, and ask for a repair, replacement or refund. If the maker is dragging its feet, point out that its warranty limits only count if it gives you a fast, reasonable way to get the repair.
rules.script_hint: Maryland Commercial Law 2-316.1 makes "as is" and warranty disclaimers unenforceable on consumer goods. And if your warranty limits don't come with a reasonable and expeditious way to get this fixed, those limits don't hold either.

rules.title: California: makers must keep parts and repair manuals available for up to 7 years
rules.window_note: Counted from when the maker last built your model, not from when you bought it, so an old model may already be past it. The rules started 1 July 2024 and cover products made after 1 July 2021. Game consoles and alarm/fire systems are excluded. So a model that's still on shelves buys you much longer than 7 years. If they refuse, get the refusal in writing — the refusal itself is the thing worth complaining about. Laws are live in California, New York, Minnesota, Oregon and Colorado. Game consoles are left out almost everywhere, and New York leaves out fridges, ovens, microwaves and HVAC.
rules.what_you_get: Spare parts, tools and the service manuals needed to fix your electronics or appliance, available to you and to independent repair shops on fair terms and at the same cost the maker charges its own approved shops. Documents must be free apart from real printing and postage costs. 7 years for anything with a wholesale price of $100 or more, 3 years for $50 to $99.99.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker's support line for the part and the service manual, or ask a local independent repair shop to order them for you. If the maker refuses, say California's Right to Repair Act requires it and that a city attorney, district attorney or the Attorney General can enforce it.
rules.script_hint: California's Right to Repair Act requires you to supply parts, tools and repair documents on fair and reasonable terms for 7 years after this model was last made. Please send me the part and the service manual.

rules.title: New York: makers must hand over parts, tools and repair manuals
rules.window_note: In force since 28 December 2023. Covers gadgets first made and first sold in New York on or after 1 July 2023. Cars, medical devices, farm and off-road gear and e-bikes are not covered. No deadline tied to when you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: The parts, tools and repair information you or a local shop need to fix your device. Repair documents at no charge, and parts and tools at the same cost the maker charges its own approved repair shops. Any contract wording that tries to dodge this duty is void.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker's support for the part and the repair manual, in writing. If they refuse, file a complaint with the New York Attorney General's Consumer Frauds Bureau.
rules.script_hint: New York's Digital Fair Repair Act, General Business Law 399-nn, says you have to give owners and independent shops the same parts, tools and manuals you give your approved repairers. Please send them.

rules.title: Oregon: makers can't use software to block a working replacement part
rules.window_note: In force since 1 January 2025. Covers phones first made and sold from 1 July 2021, and other consumer electronics from 1 July 2015. Important catch: the Attorney General can only fine companies for violations happening on or after 1 July 2027, so before then this is a strong argument rather than an instant penalty. Cars, medical gear, heating and cooling, solar, game consoles and electric toothbrushes are excluded. Fingerprint and face-unlock sensors are the one carve-out. Check the date your device was made or first sold, then say that to the maker in writing.
rules.what_you_get: Parts, tools and manuals on fair terms, at the best price the maker gives its own approved shops. Plus, for gear first made and sold after 1 January 2025, the maker cannot use software "parts pairing" to stop a good replacement part working, to slow your device down, or to nag you with warnings about unidentified parts that you can't dismiss.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker, or get your repair shop to ask, for the part and for the software or tool needed to make that part work. If a fitted part is being blocked, throttled or flagged, say so in writing and complain to the Oregon Department of Justice.
rules.script_hint: Oregon's right to repair law bans using parts pairing to block or throttle a working replacement part, or to show warnings I can't dismiss. Please give me the tool to pair this part.

rules.title: Colorado: parts, tools and manuals for your electronics, and no software lock-outs
rules.window_note: In force since 1 January 2026, covering digital electronics first made and sold or used in Colorado on or after 1 July 2021. The parts-pairing ban covers gear first made and sold in Colorado after 1 January 2026. Cars, boats, aviation, most medical devices and game consoles are excluded.
rules.what_you_get: Parts, tools and repair documentation from the maker, on request. For newer gear the maker also can't use software parts pairing to block a replacement part, reduce how well the device works, or show misleading warnings about unidentified parts. Refusing is a deceptive trade practice under Colorado law.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker in writing for the part, tool or manual. If they refuse, tell them that failing to comply is a deceptive trade practice under Colorado's right-to-repair statutes, and report it to the Colorado Attorney General.
rules.script_hint: Colorado's Consumer Right to Repair law requires you to give me the parts, tools and documentation to fix this, and failing to do so is a deceptive trade practice. Please supply them.

rules.title: Colorado: powered wheelchair makers must let you or a local shop repair it
rules.window_note: In force since 1 January 2023. No time limit tied to when you got the chair.
rules.what_you_get: Parts, embedded software, firmware, tools and repair manuals for your powered wheelchair, given to you or to an independent repair shop so you don't have to wait on the manufacturer. Any contract wording signed from 2023 onwards that tries to take this away is void and unenforceable.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the manufacturer in writing for the specific part, software, tool or manual you or your repair shop needs. If they refuse, tell them it's a deceptive trade practice under Colorado law and report it to the Colorado Attorney General.
rules.script_hint: Colorado law requires powered wheelchair makers to give owners and independent repairers the parts, software, tools and manuals needed for repairs, and refusing is a deceptive trade practice. Please send them.

rules.title: Paid by credit card? You can refuse to pay for a faulty item
rules.window_note: Only works while you still owe money on that purchase, so act before you've paid the card off. You must genuinely try to sort it out with the shop first. Usually the item must have cost more than $50 and been bought in your state or within 100 miles of your home, but those two limits drop away if the card is the shop's own card, the shop and card company are connected, or the card company mailed you the offer.
rules.what_you_get: You can stop paying your card company for a faulty item, up to the amount still owed on that purchase plus the interest charged on it. This works even when the shop refuses to help, because you're raising the same complaint against the card company that you have against the shop.
rules.how_to_claim: First genuinely try to get the shop to repair, replace or refund it, and keep a record of what you asked and what they said. Then write to your card company, explain the item is faulty, say you are asserting your claims and defences, and ask them to hold that amount off your bill.
rules.script_hint: I'm asserting my claims and defences under the Fair Credit Billing Act. The item is faulty, I made a good faith attempt to resolve it with the merchant, and I'm withholding payment on that amount.

rules.title: Quebec: your stuff has to last a reasonable time
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. How long is 'long enough' depends on what you paid, what the seller promised, and how you used it — a $1,500 TV is expected to last longer than an $850 one. It covers used items too, and it still applies even if the receipt says 'sold as is', 'final sale' or 'no warranty'. Quebec's consumer office and the courts commonly treat a fridge as roughly a 7-year product. Quebec's consumer office (OPC) will walk you through the letter for free A $2,500 fridge dying at four years is a strong case; a $60 kettle dying at four years is not.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, a swap for a working one, or your money back — even after the maker's own warranty has run out. This legal warranty is automatic and costs nothing.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the store in writing that the item stopped working too soon and that you are using the legal warranty. You can go to the store OR straight to the manufacturer — a store is not allowed to make you phone the manufacturer first. Say which you want: repair, replacement or refund. Keep your receipt. If they say no, send a formal demand letter with a deadline, then file at Quebec's Small Claims Court.
rules.script_hint: Sections 37 and 38 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act say this should still be working for a reasonable time. I'm asking you to repair, replace or refund it at no cost to me.

rules.title: Quebec: 3 to 6 years of free repair on appliances and electronics
rules.window_note: Starts 5 October 2026, and only covers new items bought or leased long-term on or after that date. How long you get depends on the item: stove, fridge, freezer, air conditioner or heat pump — 6 years; washer, dryer or dishwasher — 5 years; TV — 4 years; laptop or desktop computer, games console, cellphone or tablet — 3 years. Brand and price don't matter.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair if it stops working properly. Parts, labour and reasonable transport costs are all covered — you pay nothing.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the store you bought it from or straight to the manufacturer; either one has to honour it. Say the item is inside the warranty of good working order and ask them to repair it at no charge. Damage you caused, and normal upkeep like cleaning filters, are not covered.
rules.script_hint: This is inside Quebec's warranty of good working order, so the repair — parts, labour and transport — is free.

rules.title: Quebec: spare parts and repairs have to be available
rules.window_note: Lasts a 'reasonable time' after you buy — there is no fixed number of months. The only way a seller escapes this is by telling you in writing, before you bought, that there would be no parts or repairs. Stronger rules (fair prices, no software tricks that block repair) start 5 October 2026.
rules.what_you_get: The store or the manufacturer has to be able to sell you the replacement part, do the repair, and hand over the repair information. Parts must cost a fair price and be fittable with ordinary tools without wrecking the item. If they can't supply any of it and never warned you in writing, they pay for the repair.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the store or the manufacturer for the part or the repair. If they can't supply it, say you were never given written notice before you bought, so the repair is at their expense. They then have 10 days to come back to you with a repair plan.
rules.script_hint: You never told me in writing before I bought this that parts wouldn't be available, so under Quebec's availability warranty this repair is on you.

rules.title: Quebec: every repair comes with 3 months of free re-repair
rules.window_note: The 3 months run from the day the repair was finished — not from when you bought the item. So a repair done years after purchase still gets its own fresh 3 months.
rules.what_you_get: If the same problem comes back within 3 months of a repair, whoever did the repair has to do it again for free. Parts and labour both included.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the same repair shop with the repair invoice and say the same fault has returned inside the 3-month repair warranty. Do not pay again.
rules.script_hint: You repaired this less than three months ago and the exact same fault is back, so under Quebec law the re-repair is free — parts and labour.

rules.title: New Brunswick: you can go after the maker, not just the shop
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. How long a product should last is judged from what it is, whether it was new or used, and how you actually used and looked after it.
rules.what_you_get: New Brunswick law says products must be decent quality and last a reasonable time, sellers cannot sign those promises away, and you can claim against a company you never bought from directly — including the manufacturer.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the shop and to the manufacturer at the same time. Say New Brunswick's Consumer Product Warranty and Liability Act gives you a durability warranty that cannot be excluded, and that section 23 lets you claim even without a contract with them. Ask for repair, replacement or your money back.
rules.script_hint: Under New Brunswick's Consumer Product Warranty and Liability Act this had to be durable for a reasonable time, and I don't need a contract with you to make that claim.

rules.title: Ontario: 'no refunds, no warranty' small print doesn't beat the law
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. Ontario's promises are that goods are of sellable quality and fit for what you bought them for — judged case by case, not by a set number of months.
rules.what_you_get: The quality promises in Ontario's Sale of Goods Act automatically apply to anything you buy, lease or trade as a consumer. Any contract term that cancels those promises, or that caps how much you can claim, is not allowed.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the seller. Say Ontario's Consumer Protection Act makes the Sale of Goods Act conditions and warranties apply to your purchase, and bans any term that takes them away or puts a dollar limit on your claim. Ask for repair, replacement or refund. Small claims court if they refuse.
rules.script_hint: Ontario's Consumer Protection Act says the Sale of Goods Act warranties apply here, and a term that cancels them or caps my claim isn't allowed.

rules.title: UK: 30 days to reject a faulty item for a full refund
rules.window_note: 30 days, counted from the day after you owned it, got it, and had it installed (if it needed installing). Shorter for things that go off quickly, like food.
rules.what_you_get: Your money back in full — not a credit note, not a repair — if the item is faulty, doesn't match how it was described, or isn't fit for the job you told the seller about.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the shop that sold it (not the manufacturer) within 30 days and say clearly, in writing if you can, that you are rejecting the goods. Ask for a full refund. Don't let them push you into a repair — that's your choice, not theirs, inside 30 days.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: I'm exercising my short-term right to reject under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. The goods are faulty and I'd like a full refund, please.

rules.title: UK: one failed repair and you can demand your money back
rules.window_note: Use this once the first 30 days have passed. Within the first 6 months the shop cannot knock anything off your refund for the use you've had (cars are the one exception); after 6 months they can deduct something. Starts the moment the shop has had one go at fixing it or swapping it and the item is still faulty. You do not have to accept a second attempt.
rules.what_you_get: The shop gets ONE go at repairing or replacing it — free, reasonably quickly, and without a lot of hassle for you. If that one attempt fails, you can either keep the item and get money back off the price, or hand it back for a refund.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the shop in writing for a repair or replacement. Keep the date. If the same fault comes back, or they drag it out, write again saying the repair has failed and you are now using your final right to reject and want a refund.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: The repair has failed, so under section 24 of the Consumer Rights Act I'm using my final right to reject and asking for a refund.

rules.title: UK: 14 days to send back anything bought online
rules.window_note: 14 days from the day the goods land in your hands. If you ordered several things in one go, the clock starts when the last one arrives. If it comes in separate lots, it starts with the last lot.
rules.what_you_get: You can cancel an online, phone or doorstep purchase and get your money back, even if there's nothing wrong with the item. Useful when something arrives dead and you'd rather have the cash than argue about a repair.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller you are cancelling within 14 days of delivery — email is fine, and get it in writing. Then send the goods back and ask for your refund.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: I'm cancelling under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013. The goods arrived on [date], so I'm inside the 14-day cancellation period.

rules.title: EU: choosing repair adds a year to your guarantee
rules.window_note: Applies to goods bought on or after 31 July 2026. The extra year is added once only, even if the item gets repaired several times, and it covers the whole product — not just the bit that was fixed. A few countries have chosen to give longer.
rules.what_you_get: If you pick repair instead of replacement under the legal guarantee, your guarantee gets 12 more months. A 2-year guarantee becomes 3. The seller also has to tell you about this choice before they fix anything.
rules.how_to_claim: When the seller offers you repair or replacement, say you want it repaired, and ask them to confirm in writing that your legal guarantee now runs 12 months longer and to give you the new end date.
rules.script_hint: I'm choosing repair rather than replacement, which extends my legal guarantee by another 12 months. Please confirm the new end date in writing.

rules.title: EU: makers must repair, even after the guarantee ends
rules.window_note: Runs for as long as the maker still has to supply spare parts for that product — in practice 5 to 10 years depending on the item and the part. Since 31 July 2026 it applies even to things you bought before that date.
rules.what_you_get: For washing machines, washer-dryers, fridges, dishwashers, tumble dryers, TVs, vacuum cleaners, welding equipment, smartphones, tablets, cordless phones, servers and data storage, and anything with an e-bike or e-scooter battery in it: the maker must repair it within a reasonable time and at a reasonable price, even though the guarantee has run out. They cannot refuse just because parts are pricey, or because someone else repaired it before.
rules.how_to_claim: Look on the maker's website for their repair service and their published typical repair prices — the law makes them publish both. Contact them and ask for a repair under the EU obligation to repair. If the maker is outside the EU, ask their EU importer or the shop instead.
rules.script_hint: This product is covered by the EU obligation to repair under Directive 2024/1799. Please repair it within a reasonable time at a reasonable price.

rules.title: Apple free-repair programs (check your serial number first)
rules.window_note: Most Apple programs last 3 years from the day the device was first sold, even if your normal warranty ran out years ago. A few (safety recalls) have no end date at all. Apple's list changes, so check it again whenever something breaks.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or free replacement part for a fault Apple has admitted is its own. No AppleCare needed, no receipt needed - they go by the serial number.
rules.how_to_claim: Open Apple's service programs page and see if your product is on the list. If it is, put your serial number into the checker on that program's page (Settings > General > About on an iPhone or iPad, or the Apple menu > About This Mac). If it says you're eligible, book a Genius Bar appointment or an Apple Authorised Service Provider and bring the device in.
rules.script_hint: My serial number comes up as eligible for your service program for this exact fault, so this repair should be free of charge.

rules.title: Mac mini (2023, M2) that won't turn on: free repair
rules.window_note: Covered for 3 years after the Mac mini was first sold. Only M2 Mac minis built between 16 June 2024 and 23 November 2024 count. Apple may make you get it fixed in the country you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: Apple repairs a Mac mini that has stopped powering on, free of charge, out of warranty.
rules.how_to_claim: Type the serial number (it's on the bottom of the Mac mini) into the checker on Apple's program page. If it's eligible, book a repair at an Apple Store or Apple Authorised Service Provider.
rules.script_hint: My Mac mini won't power on and its serial number is eligible for your no-power service program - this repair should be free.

rules.title: Pixel 7a swollen battery: free battery, or cash, or store credit
rules.window_note: Google says coverage lasts 3 years from the day you bought it. Not every Pixel 7a is affected - you have to be checked.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery replacement. If your phone is out of warranty you can instead take 200 USD in cash or a 300 USD Google hardware credit; if it's still in warranty the cash option is 456 USD. Signs to look for: the phone looks fatter, the back is bulging or lifting away, or the battery drains very fast.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to g.co/pixel/7abattery and register your phone. Google runs an eligibility check and a physical inspection. Free battery swaps are done at walk-in repair centres in the US, Canada, UK, Germany, Japan, Singapore, Australia, France and India, or by post in the US and India.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 7a battery is swelling and I want to register for your extended repair programme for the 7a battery.

rules.title: Sony CEA-G CFexpress Type A cards: free repair until 2029
rules.window_note: Sony started this free repair programme on 26 June 2024 and says it runs until 29 June 2029. It doesn't matter how old the card is, only whether its serial number is on the list.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair for CEA-G80T, CEA-G160T, CEA-G320T and CEA-G640T memory cards that stop being recognised, or fail to finish saving a photo, when it's very cold (around -10C).
rules.how_to_claim: Read the 8 or 9 digit number printed on the back of the card and put it into Sony's serial number checker on the notice page. If it's affected, back up and then erase everything on the card (the repair wipes it) and take or send it to your local Sony service centre.
rules.script_hint: My CEA-G CFexpress card's serial number is on your free repair list - please repair it under that programme.

rules.title: US: free recall fixes for cars, car seats, tyres and vehicle gear
rules.window_note: The lookup tool doesn't show recalls that have already been fixed, or ones more than 15 years old.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair from a dealer for any open safety recall on your vehicle, plus recall listings for car seats, tyres and vehicle equipment.
rules.how_to_claim: Put your VIN (the 17-character number on the dashboard by the windscreen, or on your registration) into the lookup tool on the NHTSA recalls page. Anything listed as an open recall, ring your brand's dealer and book it in. You can also search car seats, tyres and equipment by make and model.
rules.script_hint: My VIN shows an open safety recall - I'd like to book the free recall repair.

rules.title: EU: search Safety Gate for dangerous product alerts
rules.window_note: No deadline. Alerts are added weekly across all EU countries.
rules.what_you_get: Confirmation that your product was flagged as dangerous somewhere in the EU, with the brand, model and the risk - useful proof when you ask the seller or maker for a free fix or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Search the European Commission's Safety Gate alerts site for your brand and model. If it appears, take the alert to whoever sold it to you and ask what they are doing for owners.
rules.script_hint: My model appears in the EU Safety Gate alerts - what are you offering owners of this product?

rules.title: AppleCare+: free new battery once yours drops under 80%
rules.window_note: Any time your AppleCare+ plan is still running. A one-off AppleCare+ plan is usually 2 years; a monthly plan keeps going until you cancel it. Only the battery that came in the box counts. Mac plans are usually 3 years. On a Mac hold Option, click the Apple menu, choose System Information, then Power. Ask for battery service under AppleCare+.
rules.what_you_get: A brand new battery fitted for free. No service fee, no parts charge.
rules.how_to_claim: On an iPhone open Settings, tap Battery, then Battery Health, and read Maximum Capacity. If it says under 80%, book a free appointment at an Apple Store or an Apple Authorised Service Provider and bring the device.
rules.script_hint: My AppleCare+ is still active and Battery Health shows maximum capacity below 80%, so the battery replacement is covered at no extra charge.

rules.title: Apple's free 1-year warranty covers a broken battery, not a tired one
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. This is the free warranty everyone gets, separate from AppleCare+. In the EU and UK your legal rights run longer than Apple's own year.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery replacement, but only if the battery is genuinely faulty: it swells, leaks, shuts the device off suddenly, or will not charge at all. Slowly holding less charge is called normal ageing and is not covered here.
rules.how_to_claim: Book a free Genius Bar or Apple Authorised Service Provider appointment inside the first year. Describe the actual failure (sudden shutdowns, swelling, refuses to charge) rather than saying the battery runs down faster than it used to.
rules.script_hint: This isn't normal ageing. It shuts down at 40% / the back has swollen / it won't take a charge at all. That's a defect in materials or workmanship, which the one-year warranty covers.

rules.title: Samsung: battery is covered if it falls under 80% or leaks
rules.window_note: Usually one year from purchase for recent Galaxy phones, tablets and watches, though the exact length depends on the model. Accessories in the box get a shorter period.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery replacement if the battery drops below 80% of the capacity it is rated for, or if it leaks, while still inside the warranty period.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the phone with your receipt to a Samsung walk-in service centre, or start a mail-in repair on Samsung's support site, and ask them to test the battery capacity.
rules.script_hint: Samsung's own warranty says batteries are covered if capacity falls below 80% of rated capacity. Please test mine and replace it under warranty.

rules.title: Your 3-year laptop probably only has a 1-year battery
rules.window_note: One year from purchase, even if the laptop itself has a 3-year or 5-year plan. The battery clock runs on its own. Some people bought a longer battery option at checkout, so check your order.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery if it fails inside that first year. After that you pay, unless you bought extended battery coverage at the same time as the laptop.
rules.how_to_claim: Run the maker's built-in battery test (Dell SupportAssist, or the battery health screen on your machine), save the result, then contact support with your service tag or serial number.
rules.script_hint: I know my system warranty is longer. I'm claiming on the separate one-year battery warranty and my machine is still inside it. Here is the failed battery test result.

rules.title: DEWALT replaces worn-out parts free for the first year
rules.window_note: The first 12 months after you buy the tool. The separate 3-year warranty covers faults, but only this first year covers parts that simply wore out. After that, worn parts are on you. The limited warranty rejects wear. The free service contract is the one that covers it.
rules.what_you_get: DEWALT services the tool and replaces parts worn out by normal use, for free. This is unusual: most brands never cover worn parts at all. There is also a 90-day money-back guarantee if you are not happy with how the tool performs.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the tool and your receipt to a DEWALT factory or authorised service centre and ask for the one-year free service contract, not a warranty repair.
rules.script_hint: I'm not claiming a defect. I'm asking for the one-year free service contract, which covers maintaining the tool and replacing parts worn by normal use.

rules.title: Makita: 3 years on lithium tools and batteries, 1 year on everything else
rules.window_note: Three years from purchase for lithium-ion tools, batteries and chargers. Everything else Makita sells is one year. Repairs needed because of normal wear and tear are never covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the tool, battery or charger has a fault in its parts or in how it was made.
rules.how_to_claim: Send or take the complete tool, battery or charger with proof of purchase to a Makita factory or authorised service centre.
rules.script_hint: This is a lithium-ion battery, so it has the three-year warranty, and it's a defect, not wear. Please repair or replace it.

rules.title: RYOBI ONE+ batteries carry a 3-year warranty of their own
rules.window_note: Three years from the date you bought the battery. If the battery came inside a tool kit, the kit receipt covers it.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery if it fails from a fault in its parts or workmanship inside three years.
rules.how_to_claim: Bring the battery with proof of purchase to a RYOBI authorised service centre, or contact RYOBI support through their website.
rules.script_hint: This 18V ONE+ battery has its own three-year limited warranty and it's still inside it. It won't take a charge any more.

rules.title: EU phones sold since June 2025 must survive 800 charges at 80%
rules.window_note: Applies to smartphones and tablets put on the EU market from 20 June 2025 onwards. Spare parts must stay available for at least 7 years after the model stops being sold.
rules.what_you_get: A strong argument, not an automatic payout. EU law now says the battery must still hold 80% of its capacity after 800 full charges. If yours is far below that after far fewer charges, it falls short of what the law requires, which supports a repair or replacement claim against the seller.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the shop that sold you the phone (not the manufacturer), say the battery does not meet the EU ecodesign endurance requirement, and ask for a free repair or replacement.
rules.script_hint: Under EU ecodesign rules this phone's battery should still hold 80% capacity after 800 full charges. Mine is well below that after far fewer, so the goods are not as they should be.

rules.title: The parts meant to wear out are the ones nobody covers
rules.window_note: This exclusion applies for the whole life of the product. It is the single most common reason a claim gets turned down, so check it before you spend time claiming. Milwaukee, for example, spells out that carbon brushes, chucks, seals, O-rings, bumpers and driver blades are normal wear items and are not covered, and every other maker words it much the same way. Instead, buy the replacement part, which is usually cheap, and fit it.
rules.what_you_get: An honest 'probably nothing' — and a way to reframe it. Makers name these parts and refuse them outright: motor brushes, chucks, cords, saw shoes, blade clamps, o-rings, seals, bumpers, driver blades, pistons, air filters and drive belts. But if the part broke or failed early rather than gradually wearing down, that is a defect, and defects ARE covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Before claiming, ask yourself: did it wear away smoothly over time, or did it fail? If it failed, say so plainly and describe how — cracked, snapped, leaked, seized — and how little use it had.
rules.script_hint: This part didn't wear out. It failed after very light use, and that's a defect in materials or workmanship, not normal wear.

rules.title: Trek covers your bike frame for as long as you own it
rules.window_note: No time limit if you are the first owner. If you bought the bike second-hand, you still get 3 years from the day the first owner bought it. Paint, Bontrager parts and wheels with metal rims run out after 2 years.
rules.what_you_get: A new frame or front fork, free, if yours cracks or fails because it was badly made. Bontrager carbon wheels are covered for life too.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the bike and your receipt into any Trek shop and ask them to open a warranty claim with Trek. Only a Trek shop can start one.
rules.script_hint: My Trek frame has cracked. Trek covers frames for the lifetime of the original owner - can you open a warranty claim for me?

rules.title: Specialized frames are covered for life if you registered the bike
rules.window_note: Lifetime only if you registered the bike, frameset or Roval wheels on Specialized's site within 90 days of buying it. If you did not register it, you get 2 years. Second owners get 2 years from the first sale.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement frame or fork if it fails because it was badly made. Paint, Specialized-branded parts and e-bike motors get 2 years. Turbo e-bike batteries get 2 years or 300 charges, whichever comes first.
rules.how_to_claim: Bring the part and the original receipt to a Specialized shop. If you bought it on specialized.com, message Rider Care instead.
rules.script_hint: My Specialized frame has failed and I registered it within 90 days of buying it, so it has the lifetime frame warranty. Please start a claim.

rules.title: Crashed your Specialized? They sell you a new frame cheap
rules.window_note: Frames and framesets have no time limit. Helmets, shoes, carbon bars, stems, seatposts, cranks, saddles and Turbo batteries and motors are covered for 5 years. Second-hand owners qualify too, as long as you have a receipt.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement or repair at a big discount when you broke it yourself riding, so a warranty will not help. You pay 35% of the price if the item is under 3 years old, 25% at 3-4 years, and 20% after that. Turbo motor and battery parts can go as low as 50% off, dropping with age.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the damaged part and any proof of purchase (receipt, bank or card statement) to a Specialized shop and ask for Assisted Replacement. It only covers damage that happened while riding, not scratches.
rules.script_hint: I crashed and damaged this - I know it is not a warranty claim. Can you put it through Specialized's Assisted Replacement programme?

rules.title: Giant and Liv bike frames have no time limit
rules.window_note: No time limit on the frame for the first owner. Downhill frames get 3 years, rigid forks 10 years, Giant-branded parts 2 years, paint 1 year. It does not pass on to whoever you sell the bike to.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement frame if it fails because it was badly made, plus free parts and some labour money for the shop. E-bike batteries and electric parts are covered for 2 years, or 600 charges for the battery.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the bike and your receipt to a Giant shop. They have to see the bike in person - photos by email will not do.
rules.script_hint: My Giant frame has failed. Giant gives the original owner a lifetime frame warranty - here is my receipt, can you file it?

rules.title: Cannondale frames are covered for life if the bike is registered
rules.window_note: No time limit on frames from the 2026 model year onward, but only if the bike was registered on cannondale.com or by the shop. Older Cannondales have their own rules, so ask the shop which set applies. Paint and Cannondale-branded parts get 1 year. It does not pass to a new owner.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement frame, swing arm, chainstay or seatstay if it fails because it was badly made. Lefty and Headshok fork bodies are covered for life too.
rules.how_to_claim: Clean the bike, then take it with the original dated receipt to a Cannondale shop on the same continent where you bought it.
rules.script_hint: My Cannondale frame has failed. The bike is registered with Cannondale, so the frame has lifetime cover - please open a claim.

rules.title: Brompton frames get 7 years if you registered the bike
rules.window_note: 7 years from the day it was sold if you registered it in the My Brompton area of their site. Only 2 years if you never registered it. There is no mileage limit either way.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of the main frame parts if they fail because they were badly made. Other non-wearing parts like crank arms, brake calipers and mudguards get 2 years. Electric Brompton parts get 2 years, or 3 if registered.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the shop that sold you the bike, or contact Brompton, with your frame number and receipt.
rules.script_hint: My Brompton main frame has failed and the bike is registered on My Brompton, so it has 7-year cover. Can you start a warranty claim?

rules.title: Britax: 1 year on car seats, 2 years on strollers
rules.window_note: Car seats are covered for 1 year from the day you bought them. Strollers get 2 years. Both start from the original purchase date, and you need the receipt. Damage from misuse or from not following the manual isn't covered.
rules.what_you_get: Britax repairs the item or sends you free replacement parts if something was badly made.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Britax Consumer Services with your receipt and the model and date-of-manufacture label on the seat or stroller. Lines are open weekdays 10am-4pm Eastern.
rules.script_hint: My Britax stroller has a fault and it is less than 2 years old. I have the receipt - can you send replacement parts under warranty?

rules.title: Graco replaces a faulty car seat or stroller free for 1 year
rules.window_note: 1 year from the day you bought it or the day it was delivered, whichever is later. Second-hand items are not covered. For most Graco gear you must have bought it from Graco or a shop they approve of, but that limit does not apply to car seats and carriers.
rules.what_you_get: A brand-new product or a brand-new part, free, if yours was badly made. If your model is gone they send something similar of the same or higher value.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Graco or fill in their warranty claim form. Have the item number, serial number, date stamp, receipt and photos ready.
rules.script_hint: My Graco is under a year old and this part broke on its own. I have the receipt and photos - I would like a free replacement under the limited warranty.

rules.title: A recalled car seat must be fixed, swapped or refunded free
rules.window_note: No purchase window, and it does not matter whether you ever registered the seat or kept the receipt. The free-fix duty only stops for things bought more than 15 years before the recall notice, and car seats expire long before that. Free, including posting you the fix kit. Free recall fixes don't expire and don't depend on you having the receipt.
rules.what_you_get: By US law the maker has to put it right for free - repair it, swap it for the same or an equal seat, or refund what you paid. The maker picks which one.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the model number and date of manufacture on the sticker on the seat, look it up on the government recall list, then call the maker and say your seat is on it. Registering your seat also gets you told automatically next time.
rules.script_hint: My car seat, model number [X] made on [date], is on the recall list. The law says the remedy is free - please send me the fix or a replacement.

rules.title: Big Agnes fixes faults for life and other damage for a small fee
rules.window_note: No time limit on manufacturing faults, for the life of the product. Electronics are the exception at 2 years with a receipt. You must have bought it from Big Agnes or a shop they approve of.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if a seam, stitch or material was faulty. If it is just damaged or worn out - small holes, rips, split zipper sliders, broken poles, bent hardware - they will usually repair it for a small fee rather than make you buy new.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a case on the Big Agnes support site or call them, then send the item in clean and dry.
rules.script_hint: The zipper slider on my Big Agnes tent has split. If that is not a warranty fault, can you quote me for a repair instead?

rules.title: MSR tents and stoves: 3 years on faults
rules.window_note: 3 years from purchase, for the first owner only, and only if you looked after the gear. Normal wear, punctures, scrapes and sun damage do not count.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the tent, stove or filter was faulty. They try to fix it first and will often just post you the replacement part with instructions.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact MSR through Cascade Designs and attach your receipt, a clear description of the problem, and photos - photos speed it up a lot.
rules.script_hint: My MSR tent has a fault and it is under 3 years old. Photos and receipt attached - can you repair or replace it under warranty?

rules.title: NEMO covers its gear for as long as it lasts
rules.window_note: No time limit, but you must be the first owner and have a receipt from a shop NEMO approves of. Gear bought second-hand or at a garage sale is not covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if something was made wrong - loose seams, thin or missing insulation, bad construction. Return postage back to you inside the US and Canada is free.
rules.how_to_claim: File a claim on NEMO's site and wait for a return number. Wash and dry the item first - they will not inspect dirty gear - then post it to them with the number in the box. Expect 2 to 6 weeks.
rules.script_hint: The seams on my NEMO sleeping bag have come apart. NEMO's guarantee has no time limit for the original owner - here is my receipt.

rules.title: Therm-a-Rest pads are covered for life against faults
rules.window_note: No time limit on faults for the first owner, buying from an approved shop. Electronics are the exception at 2 years. Punctures, scrapes and general wear are not faults.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the pad, bag or pillow was badly made. They repair first where they can. A mattress over two years old may come back as a similar-looking one instead. If your damage is not a fault, they will often still repair it for a fair fee.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Therm-a-Rest through Cascade Designs with your receipt, a description, and photos so they can identify the model.
rules.script_hint: My Therm-a-Rest is leaking along a seam, not from a puncture. Photos and receipt attached - can you repair or replace it?

rules.title: Casper mattress sagging more than an inch: 10-year cover
rules.window_note: 10 years from purchase. Only the first buyer is covered - it does not pass on. Clearance and final-sale mattresses can have a shorter warranty, so check the label.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the mattress has a visible dip deeper than 1 inch, the foam splits or cracks, or the cover zip is faulty. If it has to be shipped back, Casper covers that cost.
rules.how_to_claim: Email Casper with your proof of purchase and photos. A tape measure or ruler laid across the dip in the photo makes the claim much easier to approve.
rules.script_hint: My Casper mattress has a dip deeper than one inch, measured with a ruler in these photos. That is a covered defect under the 10-year warranty.

rules.title: Purple mattress dipping more than an inch: 10-year cover
rules.window_note: 10 years from purchase, first buyer only. The cover is separate and only gets 2 years. After the first 100 days you pay the shipping. Do not take the cover off to inspect it - that can cancel the warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the mattress has a dip deeper than 1 inch that stays after you get off it, or if the material cracks or splits during normal use.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Purple with your proof of purchase and photos showing the dip measured against the flat area around it. Leave the cover on.
rules.script_hint: My Purple mattress has a body impression deeper than one inch after full recovery. That is listed as a defect in the 10-year warranty - please open a claim.

rules.title: Tempur-Pedic: 10 years, no deductible
rules.window_note: 10 years from the purchase date on your receipt, first buyer only - it does not pass to anyone you sell it to. Keep the receipt for the full 10 years. If they replace it, the new one keeps the original date, it does not restart.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of a faulty mattress or flat foundation, covering every part, with nothing to pay towards it. You pay only the transport cost.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Tempur-Pedic and send a copy of the receipt, a written description of what is wrong, and photos (or a recording if the problem is a noise). They may ask for proof that the base or frame under the mattress was a proper one.
rules.script_hint: My Tempur-Pedic mattress has a defect and it is inside the 10-year limited warranty. Receipt and photos attached - please arrange a repair or replacement.

rules.title: IKEA mattresses have a 10-year warranty most people forget
rules.window_note: 10 years from the day you bought it, first buyer only. It does not cover kids' mattresses, mattress pads or toppers, mattress protectors, or sofa-bed mattresses.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or the same or a comparable mattress, if the seams split, springs are damaged, the handles or base break, or it sags badly. IKEA pays for parts, labour and the repair staff's travel.
rules.how_to_claim: Take or send your original receipt to your local IKEA store - the receipt is the proof of purchase and the claim will not work without it. IKEA inspects it and decides between repair and replacement.
rules.script_hint: My IKEA mattress is sagging badly and it is under 10 years old. IKEA gives mattresses a 10-year limited warranty - here is my receipt.

rules.title: Chase Sapphire Reserve buys it back when the store won't take a return

rules.script_hint: The store refused to take this back and I bought it under 90 days ago on my Chase Sapphire Reserve. I'd like to use return protection.

rules.script_hint: I pay my phone bill with my Chase Freedom Flex and my screen cracked. I want to file a cell phone protection claim.

rules.script_hint: I'm filing a cell phone protection claim on my Chase Freedom Flex. I pay my monthly wireless bill with this card and my phone was damaged/stolen on this date.

rules.script_hint: I bought this on my Capital One World Elite Mastercard and found it advertised cheaper within 120 days. I want to file a price protection claim.

rules.title: UK Section 75: your credit card company owes you exactly what the shop owes you
rules.window_note: The law itself sets no cut-off. In practice people claim up to about six years after the thing went wrong, because six years is the normal court deadline for a broken deal in England and Wales. Don't wait — ask as soon as you spot the problem. If they turn you down, take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Debit cards do not count - for those, ask about chargeback instead.
rules.what_you_get: This is the biggest unused right in Britain. If you put a purchase on a credit card, your card company is on the hook for exactly the same things the shop is. Faulty, never turned up, or not what you were promised? Ask the card company for a repair, a replacement or your money back. It still works if the shop has gone bust, moved on, or is simply ignoring you. It covers anything with a ticket price over £100 and up to £30,000. It does NOT work with debit cards, charge cards, overdrafts, bank transfers or cash — and note that some American Express cards are charge cards rather than credit cards, so check yours. Pay even a tiny slice — a £20 deposit on a £3,000 kitchen — and the card company is still on the hook for the whole thing.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone or message your credit card company (not the shop) and say you are making a Section 75 claim. Send them the receipt, whatever you were promised in the advert or listing, and photos of what is wrong. They have to investigate it themselves — they are not allowed to just tell you to go back to the shop.
rules.script_hint: I'm making a Section 75 claim under the Consumer Credit Act 1974. The cash price was over £100 and I paid at least part of it on this credit card, so you are jointly and severally liable with the seller. I want a repair, a replacement, or my money back.

rules.title: UK Section 75A: the backup rule for things costing more than £30,000
rules.window_note: No fixed legal deadline, but treat six years from the problem as your practical limit. You also need to have tried the seller first, so start that straight away.
rules.what_you_get: If something cost more than £30,000 — up to £60,260 — Section 75 is too small for it, but Section 75A can still catch it. It applies when you paid with a loan the seller arranged for you, and it lets you make the lender put things right. It is one step weaker than Section 75: you have to have genuinely tried the seller first and got nowhere (including because they have gone bust, vanished, or won't reply).
rules.how_to_claim: First chase the seller and keep every email and letter as proof you tried. If they go bust, save the news or the Companies House page. Then write to the lender saying you are making a Section 75A claim and attach that proof.
rules.script_hint: I'm making a claim under Section 75A of the Consumer Credit Act 1974. I've taken reasonable steps to pursue the supplier and have not obtained satisfaction, so I'm asking you as the lender under the linked credit agreement to put this right.

rules.title: Chargeback: your bank claws the money back — and it works on debit cards too
rules.window_note: Usually about 120 days — roughly four months — counted from the day you should have received the thing, or the day you discovered it was broken or not as described. Some cases get longer, some shorter, so ring the bank the same week you notice.
rules.what_you_get: Your bank asks the seller's bank to hand the money back. Unlike Section 75, it works on debit cards and there is no £100 minimum, so it covers all the cheap stuff Section 75 misses. Good reasons to use it: the thing never arrived, it arrived broken, it wasn't what was described, or a refund you were promised never showed up. Your bank does not have to raise a chargeback, but if you have a fair reason it is bad practice for them to refuse.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the seller first and save the messages — banks usually want to see you tried. Then ring your bank, say you want to raise a chargeback, and give them the receipt, the messages and photos of the problem. If the first attempt is knocked back, ask them to push it again with extra evidence.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to raise a chargeback on this transaction. The goods were [never delivered / faulty / not as described], I've already contacted the seller and got nowhere, and I'm within the card scheme's time limit.

rules.title: If your UK bank says no, the Ombudsman is free — and often says yes
rules.window_note: Complain to the bank first. If eight weeks go by with no final answer, or you don't like the answer they give, take it to the Ombudsman. Don't sit on it — go soon after the bank replies, because the Ombudsman has its own deadline for taking cases on. You get 6 months from the date on the bank's final response letter to go to the ombudsman. You also normally need to have complained to the bank within 6 years of the problem, or 3 years of realising you had one. They get 8 weeks for most complaints and 15 days for payment complaints.
rules.what_you_get: A free referee. If your bank turns down your Section 75 claim, or refuses to try a chargeback, the Financial Ombudsman Service will look at it for nothing. They can order the bank to refund you in full or in part, arrange a repair or replacement, collect the goods at no cost to you, refund interest and charges, and pay you extra for the trouble and upset. Banks know this, which is why simply saying the words often gets the claim reopened.
rules.how_to_claim: Send the bank a formal complaint in writing and ask for a final response letter. Wait for their answer or for eight weeks, whichever comes first. Then fill in the free complaint form on the Ombudsman's website and attach everything you sent the bank.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to raise this as a formal complaint and receive a final response letter. If I'm not happy with it I'll be taking the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

rules.title: EU: in the first year you don't have to prove a thing
rules.window_note: Runs for one year from the day the goods were delivered. Some EU countries stretch it to two years. After it runs out you can still claim under the two-year guarantee, but then you have to show the fault was there from the beginning. If the seller says you must have broken it, or asks you to pay for a report proving the fault, tell them that within the first year the burden of proof is on them, not you. Countries are allowed to make it 24 months and some have - France is one of them.
rules.what_you_get: If a fault shows up in the first year, the law simply assumes it was already there when you got the item. You don't have to prove anything, take it to a technician, or argue about it. The seller has to prove it was fine when it left them — which is hard and expensive for them, so most just fix it. Several EU countries stretch this to a full two years.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller the fault appeared within a year of delivery, so the law treats it as having been there all along, and it is on them to prove otherwise. Then ask for the free repair or replacement. Put it in writing so there's a record of the date.
rules.script_hint: The fault appeared within one year of delivery, so under Article 11 of Directive (EU) 2019/771 it is presumed to have existed at delivery. Please repair or replace it free of charge.

rules.title: EU: if the maker promised it would last, chase the maker directly
rules.window_note: Lasts as long as the maker's own durability promise lasts — often five, ten or twenty years. Your normal two-year cover from the shop keeps running alongside it, so you can use whichever is better.
rules.what_you_get: If the manufacturer advertised that the product would last — '10-year motor guarantee', 'built to last 20 years', that kind of claim — EU law makes the manufacturer itself directly responsible to you for repairing or replacing it for the whole length of that promise. You get to skip the shop entirely and go straight to the maker. And they are not allowed to use that promise to shrink your normal legal rights.
rules.how_to_claim: Find where the maker made the promise — the box, the website, the manual, an old advert — and screenshot it before it disappears. Then contact the manufacturer directly with the screenshot and proof of purchase and ask for the repair or replacement under their guarantee of durability.
rules.script_hint: You advertise a guarantee of durability of [X] years for this product. Under Article 17 of Directive (EU) 2019/771 you are directly liable to me for repair or replacement for that entire period. Here is my proof of purchase.

rules.title: Canada: 90 days of free theft-and-damage cover on almost every credit card
rules.window_note: The item itself is covered for 90 days from the day you bought it. But once something happens you have to phone it in fast, and each bank is different: RBC and BMO want to hear from you within 30 days, CIBC and American Express within 45, TD and Scotiabank within 90. Ring the same week.
rules.what_you_get: Nearly every Canadian credit card quietly insures whatever you buy with it against theft and accidental damage for the first 90 days — free, automatic, no sign-up. Drop the new laptop down the stairs, have the new bike stolen off the porch, and the card's insurer repairs it, replaces it, or pays you back. Two catches worth knowing: it usually pays only after your home or tenant insurance does, so often you get the deductible back rather than the whole item, and used or refurbished items are excluded.
rules.how_to_claim: Search your card's exact name plus 'certificate of insurance' to find the claims number, then phone it before you pay for any repair or replacement. If it was stolen, report it to the police first and get the report number — the insurer will ask for it. Keep the store receipt and the card statement showing the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open a purchase security claim. I bought this on my card on [date], it was [stolen / accidentally damaged] on [date], and I'm still inside the 90 days.

rules.title: RBC credit cards double the maker's warranty for free
rules.window_note: The free extra cover starts the moment the maker's warranty ends and lasts as long as that warranty did, up to one extra year. The maker's warranty and RBC's extra can't add up to more than five years total. Once something breaks, tell RBC within 30 days and get your paperwork in within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: Buy something on an RBC credit card and RBC automatically doubles the manufacturer's warranty for you, up to one extra year, at no cost and with nothing to sign up for. A one-year warranty becomes two. If the thing fails during that bonus year, RBC's insurer pays to repair or replace it. Exactly what's covered mirrors the original warranty, so if the maker only repaired rather than replaced, so will RBC.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone the claims line and open a claim BEFORE you pay for any repair — paying first can void it. Have three things ready: the store receipt, the RBC statement showing the purchase, and the manufacturer's original warranty paperwork. Terms vary slightly between RBC cards, so pull up your own card's certificate of insurance too.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open an extended warranty claim on my RBC card. The manufacturer's warranty has expired but I'm still inside the extra year that RBC's Extended Warranty Insurance gives me.

rules.title: TD credit cards double the maker's warranty by up to 12 extra months
rules.window_note: TD's cover begins the day the maker's warranty runs out and lasts as long as that warranty did, capped at 12 extra months. Report a problem to TD's claims administrator within 90 days of it happening. One trap: if the maker's warranty is longer than five years, TD only covers it if you registered the item within the first year after buying it.
rules.what_you_get: TD doubles the manufacturer's warranty on things you buy with a TD credit card, up to 12 extra months, free and automatic. The warranty has to be valid in Canada. Used, refurbished and demo items are out, and so are vehicles. There's a $60,000 lifetime cap across all your TD cards combined, which almost nobody ever reaches.
rules.how_to_claim: Call TD's claims administrator before you spend anything on the repair. Bring the store receipt, the TD statement showing the purchase, the manufacturer's Canadian warranty, and a repair estimate from an authorised repair shop. Check your own card's product summary too — the Aeroplan Visa Infinite Privilege and some other TD cards differ slightly.
rules.script_hint: I'm opening an Extended Warranty Protection claim on my TD credit card. The manufacturer's warranty has expired and I'm within the additional period TD's coverage provides.

rules.title: Scotiabank cards double the maker's warranty, up to one extra year
rules.window_note: Cover starts when the maker's warranty ends and runs for the same length again, capped at one extra year. Once something goes wrong, call within 90 days and before you get anything repaired. If the maker's warranty is longer than five years, you must register the item with Scotiabank within one year of buying it or it isn't covered at all.
rules.what_you_get: Scotiabank doubles the repair cover the manufacturer gave you, up to one extra year, free, on things where you charged the full price to your Scotiabank card (Scene+ points count too). It works on items bought anywhere in the world as long as the maker's warranty is honoured in Canada or the US. You can file the claim online rather than sitting on the phone.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the claims administrator, or file online at manulife.ca/scotia, before paying for any repair. Have the store receipt, the card statement, and the manufacturer's warranty ready. Wording varies a little between Scotiabank cards, so also look up your own card's certificate of insurance.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an Extended Warranty claim on my Scotiabank card. The original manufacturer's warranty has run out and I'm within the additional year of repair coverage.

rules.title: BMO Mastercards add up to a free extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: The extension runs on from the day the maker's warranty ends, up to a maximum of one extra year. Give BMO's operations centre written notice within 30 days of the problem and send proof within 90 days. If it truly wasn't possible to do that in time, you still have up to one year to get it in. If the maker's warranty is over five years, register the item with BMO within one year of purchase.
rules.what_you_get: BMO stretches the manufacturer's warranty on things bought with a BMO Mastercard by up to one extra year, free and automatic, and it covers parts and labour for mechanical breakdown just as the original warranty did. Items bought with reward points count as long as you charged the taxes to the card. Two things to know: cover stops dead if the manufacturer goes out of business, and items sold with a lifetime warranty are excluded.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring the operations centre as soon as it breaks to get a claim form, and don't pay for the repair first. You'll need the claim form, the store receipt, the BMO statement showing the purchase, the maker's Canadian warranty, and a repair bill or estimate from an authorised repair shop.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open an Extended Warranty claim on my BMO Mastercard. The original manufacturer's warranty has expired and I'm within BMO's one-year extension.

rules.title: CIBC Visa cards double the maker's warranty, up to one extra full year
rules.window_note: The extra cover starts the moment the maker's warranty expires and doubles it, capped at one extra full year. Tell CIBC's insurer as soon as you know there's a problem, and no later than 45 days after it happens — miss that and they can turn the claim down. Then send the signed loss report within 90 days. If the maker's warranty is over five years, register the item within the first year.
rules.what_you_get: CIBC's Extended Protection automatically doubles the manufacturer's warranty on anything you charge in full to a CIBC Visa, up to one extra full year, with nothing to sign up for. It works on items bought in Canada, the US or anywhere in the world, as long as the maker's warranty is honoured in Canada or the US. Gifts you buy for other people are covered too. Used, refurbished and demo items are not.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone the claims line straight away — the 45-day clock is strict. Then send the signed loss report with ORIGINAL receipts (not photocopies): the store receipt, the Visa slip or statement, and the manufacturer's warranty.
rules.script_hint: I'm reporting an Extended Protection claim on my CIBC Visa. The manufacturer's warranty has expired and I'm inside the additional year of coverage. Please send me the loss report form.

rules.title: Quebec's new good-working-order warranty on appliances and electronics
rules.window_note: This rule only starts biting on 5 October 2026, and it runs from the day the goods are delivered to you. Quebec sets the exact length for each type of item in a separate regulation, so look up the length for your item before you claim — the law itself does not name a number.
rules.what_you_get: From 5 October 2026 Quebec gives a named list of everyday goods a built-in warranty that they will actually work: stoves, fridges, freezers, dishwashers, washing machines, dryers, TVs, desktop computers, laptops, tablets, mobile phones, games consoles, air conditioners and heat pumps. It covers parts AND labour, the shop or manufacturer has to pay the reasonable shipping costs, and — unusually — it carries over to whoever you sell the thing to second-hand. You can also choose to have it fixed by someone else and send them the bill.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the shop or the manufacturer that the item is covered by the warranty of good working order under section 38.1 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act, and that they have to cover parts, labour and shipping. If they stall, say you will have it repaired elsewhere and bill them, which the law expressly allows.
rules.script_hint: This item is covered by the warranty of good working order under section 38.1 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. Please repair it at no cost to me, including parts, labour and shipping — or confirm in writing that I may have it repaired elsewhere at your expense.

rules.title: Costco adds a free second year of warranty on TVs, computers and big appliances
rules.window_note: Covers you for 2 years from the day you bought it in the warehouse, or the day it was delivered if you ordered online. Most makers only give you 1 year, so year two is free cover you probably did not know you had. Touchscreen tablets are not included.
rules.what_you_get: Costco fixes it, replaces it, or refunds up to what you paid - their choice. Covers TVs, projectors, computers, and big appliances like fridges over 10 cubic feet, freezers, ranges, cooktops, over-the-range microwaves, dishwashers, water heaters, washers and dryers.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Costco Technical and Warranty Services. Have ready: your membership number, the item number from your receipt, the model and serial number, and the date you bought it.
rules.script_hint: I bought this at Costco and it's broken. Costco extends the maker's warranty to 2 years, and I'm still inside that - I'd like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: REI takes back anything badly made, no matter how old
rules.window_note: No deadline at all, as long as the problem is a fault in how the thing was made - a seam that came apart, a zip that failed, a buckle that snapped. Normal wear and tear does not count, and neither does damage from an accident or from using it wrong.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Wash or clean the item first - REI turns away dirty gear. Then take it to any REI store, or start a return on rei.com and say the reason is a manufacturing defect.
rules.script_hint: This has a manufacturing defect in materials or workmanship. REI's policy says those can come back at any time, whatever the purchase date.

rules.title: REI members get a full year to change their mind
rules.window_note: 365 days if you are an REI Co-op member. 90 days if you are not. Outdoor electronics - watches, GPS units, bike trainers, emergency beacons, cameras - are 90 days for everyone. Used gear bought in store is final sale.
rules.what_you_get: A swap for something else or your money back, even if you have used it, as long as you genuinely are not satisfied.
rules.how_to_claim: Clean the item, then take it to any REI store - free, and no paper receipt needed if you used your member number when you bought it. By post they take $7.99 off your refund.
rules.script_hint: I'm an REI member and this is inside my one-year satisfaction guarantee. I'd like to return it.
