rules.title: L.L.Bean: one year to change your mind, longer if it's badly made
rules.window_note: One year to send it back just because you are not happy with it. After that year they will still look at anything that is genuinely faulty - badly made or made from bad materials. Heads up: this used to be a no-limit guarantee for anything at all, and L.L.Bean tightened it in 2018, so old advice you read online may be out of date.
rules.what_you_get: Your money back inside the first year. After a year, they consider faulty items case by case.
rules.how_to_claim: Start a return on llbean.com, or take it to an L.L.Bean store with proof of purchase. If it is over a year old, say clearly that the item is defective rather than that you changed your mind.
rules.script_hint: This is defective due to materials or craftsmanship, and L.L.Bean's guarantee says you'll consider those after the one-year window.

rules.title: Nordstrom has no time limit on returns at all
rules.window_note: Nordstrom says plainly: there are no time limits for returns or exchanges. They decide each one case by case, and they do look at the condition of the item and how often you return things. There are no restocking fees. This is only the main Nordstrom stores and nordstrom.com - Nordstrom Rack is much stricter.
rules.what_you_get: A refund back to how you paid. If they cannot find any record of the sale, you get the current price on a Nordstrom gift card instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any register at a Nordstrom store, or start a return online. Bring the receipt or order number if you have it - if you do not, they can often still find the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I know this is old, but Nordstrom's policy says there's no time limit on returns. Could you take a look at it for me?

rules.title: Target's own brands come back for a whole year
rules.window_note: A full year, but only for Target's own labels - the brands you can only buy at Target. Anything else in the shop gets 90 days. One catch: designer collaborations that are only in shops for a short time get just two weeks.
rules.what_you_get: A swap for a new one, or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to the guest service desk at any Target with your receipt. If you paid through the Target app, the purchase in your Target Wallet counts as the receipt.
rules.script_hint: This is a Target owned brand, and those have a one-year return window - here's my receipt.

rules.title: Paying with the Target Circle card buys you 30 extra days
rules.window_note: Most things get 90 days at Target. Pay with the Target Circle credit or debit card, or be a Circle 360 member, and you get 30 days on top - so 120 days. It does not stack on Target's own brands, which already get a year.
rules.what_you_get: An extra 30 days to return nearly anything you bought with that card.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to guest service at any Target with the Circle card you paid with, so they can pull up the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I paid with my Target Circle card, so I get an extra 30 days on this return.

rules.title: IKEA gives you a year to return anything you never opened
rules.window_note: 365 days if the box is still sealed. 180 days if you opened it. You need the receipt and a government photo ID. They will not take plants, cut fabric, custom worktops, as-is items, or anything that is dirty, stained or altered.
rules.what_you_get: A full refund back to the way you paid.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to the returns desk at any IKEA store with the receipt and your photo ID.
rules.script_hint: This is unopened and still inside IKEA's 365-day return window - here's my receipt.

rules.title: IKEA lets you swap a mattress you don't find comfy
rules.window_note: One swap, within 90 days of buying it. Sleep on it first - that is what the window is for.
rules.what_you_get: You exchange it once for a different IKEA mattress, free.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the returns desk at any IKEA with your receipt and ask to use the Love It or Exchange It mattress swap.
rules.script_hint: This mattress isn't comfortable for me. I'd like to use IKEA's one-time mattress exchange.

rules.title: IKEA quietly covers kitchens for 25 years and mattresses for 10
rules.window_note: Kitchen cabinet frames, doors, hinges and drawers (SEKTION): 25 years. Mattresses, sofa frames and cushions, wardrobes, storage and taps: 10 years. Kitchen knives and pots and pans: 15 years. Appliances: 5 years. The clock starts the day you bought it, and you need the original receipt.
rules.what_you_get: IKEA repairs it or replaces the faulty part or product at no cost, if the problem is a fault in the materials or the way it was made. Sagging mattresses, split seams, broken springs and broken mattress bases are all covered. Normal wear, scratches, knocks and bad assembly are not.
rules.how_to_claim: Take photos of the fault, find your original receipt, and take both to the returns desk at any IKEA or call IKEA customer service. Say you are making a warranty claim, not a return.
rules.script_hint: I'm making a claim under the IKEA limited warranty on this - it's a fault in materials or workmanship, and the warranty runs for years, not months.

rules.title: Home Depot's own card turns 90 days of returns into 365
rules.window_note: A full year instead of 90 days, if you paid with a Home Depot Consumer Credit Card, a Pro Xtra Credit Card, or a Home Depot Commercial Account. It does not rescue the short-window stuff: big appliances are 48 hours, dehumidifiers and generators and air conditioners are 7 days, and furniture, TVs, computers and gas-powered garden kit are 30 days.
rules.what_you_get: A full refund, up to a year after you bought it.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any Home Depot store with your receipt, the Home Depot card you paid with, and photo ID. Any store will take it, even if you bought it online.
rules.script_hint: I paid with my Home Depot card, which gives me 365 days to return this instead of 90.

rules.title: Home Depot guarantees trees and shrubs for a year
rules.window_note: Perennials, trees, roses and shrubs are guaranteed for a full year. Other plants get 90 days. Cut flowers and floral arrangements are not covered at all.
rules.what_you_get: Store credit for the plant if it dies on you.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the dead plant (or a photo of it, plus the pot or tag) and your receipt to the garden centre desk at any Home Depot.
rules.script_hint: This shrub died. Home Depot's everyday guarantee covers perennials, trees, roses and shrubs for a year - I'd like the store credit.

rules.title: Best Buy's paid membership stretches 15 days of returns to 60
rules.window_note: 60 days if you pay for My Best Buy Plus or My Best Buy Total. Everyone else gets 15 days. Anything you activate - phones, cellular tablets, hotspots, cellular watches - is 14 days no matter what, except Verizon devices which get 30. The membership window does not apply to things sold by other sellers on the Best Buy site. These terms took effect on 23 February 2026, so check anything you read that is older.
rules.what_you_get: A refund the same way you paid, or a straight swap for the same item.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any Best Buy store with the packaging, accessories and your receipt or packing slip, or start a return in your Best Buy account for a free FedEx label. Wipe your data and unlink the device first, or they can refuse it.
rules.script_hint: I'm a My Best Buy Plus member, so my return window on this is 60 days, not 15.

rules.title: John Lewis includes 2 years of cover on electricals and 5 on TVs
rules.window_note: At least 2 years on every electrical item, and 5 years on TVs. You do not pay extra for it - it comes with the purchase. Most makers only give you 1 year, so John Lewis is covering you long after the maker has stopped.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, done by a repairer the maker approves. If it cannot be fixed, they sort out a replacement.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact John Lewis - in a shop, or through the guarantees page on their site - with your order number, and tell them the item is faulty and still inside the John Lewis guarantee.
rules.script_hint: This is faulty and it's still covered by the John Lewis guarantee that came with it - I'd like it repaired.

rules.title: Decathlon covers everything it makes for 2 years, and some gear for life
rules.window_note: 2 years on everything, counted from the day you bought it. Much longer on some things: Quechua, Forclaz and Simond rucksacks are covered 10 years, metal bike frames and forks for life, and Van Rysel carbon frames for 5 years. Decathlon also repairs gear that is out of warranty - ask, even if you are past the date.
rules.what_you_get: A repair, a swap for the same item, or your money back if they cannot fix or replace it.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your order confirmation or receipt, then take the item into a Decathlon store or contact Decathlon customer service and say it has a manufacturing fault.
rules.script_hint: This is a Decathlon product with a manufacturing defect, and Decathlon gives a 2-year warranty on all its products.

rules.title: MEC has no deadline for returning gear
rules.window_note: MEC says straight out that there is no time limit on returns of qualifying products. Electronics are the one exception - those are capped at 90 days. What they will not take: gear that is simply worn out or at the end of its life, final sale items unless they are faulty, hygiene items that have been worn, and food, fuel or bear spray.
rules.what_you_get: A refund to how you paid, or an MEC gift card.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any MEC store, or fill in the online return form on mec.ca and post it. If it is a warranty problem, message MEC Customer Care with photos before you send anything.
rules.script_hint: MEC's Rocksolid Guarantee has no time limit on returns, and this hasn't met my expectations - I'd like a refund.

rules.title: Pixel 9 Pro / 9 Pro XL line or flicker on screen - Google replaces the screen free
rules.window_note: Coverage runs for 3 years from the day you bought the phone new.
rules.what_you_get: A free screen replacement if a vertical line runs from the bottom of the screen to the top. Screen flicker also counts on the Pixel 9 Pro.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to store.google.com/repair, check your device, then book a walk-in repair centre or start a mail-in repair. A cracked screen or water damage can stop you qualifying.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 9 Pro has the vertical line on the display, which is covered by your Extended Repair Program, so the screen replacement should be at no charge.

rules.title: Pixel 8 line or flicker on screen - Google replaces the screen free
rules.window_note: Coverage runs for 3 years from the day you bought the phone new.
rules.what_you_get: One free screen replacement if your Pixel 8 shows a vertical line running up the display, or the display flickers.
rules.how_to_claim: Enter your IMEI number on Google's repair page to check you qualify, then book a walk-in or mail-in repair. Cracked glass or water damage can mean you have to pay.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 8 has the vertical line fault covered by your Extended Repair Program, so I should get a free display replacement.

rules.title: Pixel 9 Pro Fold acting up - Google may swap the whole phone free
rules.window_note: Coverage runs for 3 years from the day you bought the phone new. Replacements started going out on 8 December 2025.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement phone if your Pixel 9 Pro Fold is one of the units Google flagged as having a fault that stops it working properly.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to store.google.com/repair and check your Pixel 9 Pro Fold. If it is affected, Google arranges a replacement online, at a Google Store, or at a walk-in centre.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 9 Pro Fold is covered by your extended warranty program, so I should be eligible for a replacement at no charge.

rules.title: LG fridge stopped getting cold - the compressor is covered for 10 years
rules.window_note: Years 1-5: LG pays for the compressor part AND the labour. Years 6-10: LG still pays for the Linear or Inverter compressor part, but you pay the fitting. The clock starts on the day you bought it, so keep your receipt. Ask them to confirm in writing that the part is covered before the technician arrives. Terms vary by model, so check your own model number on LG's site. Book a repair through LG rather than a random local engineer - an outside repair can cost you the free part.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement compressor - the expensive part that makes the fridge cold. In the first 5 years the fitting is free too. The sealed system (condenser, dryer, connecting tube, evaporator) is also parts-and-labour free for 5 years.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring LG on 1-800-243-0000 and tell them the fridge is not cooling. Have your model number, serial number and proof of purchase ready. Ask them to book a warranty repair, not a paid one.
rules.script_hint: My LG fridge has stopped cooling and my Linear Inverter compressor is still inside the 10-year parts warranty, so I want this booked as a warranty repair.

rules.title: LG washing machine motor covered for 10 years
rules.window_note: The whole washer is parts-and-labour free for 1 year. After that, the Direct Drive Motor (the stator or rotor) is a free part for 10 years from the day you bought it, but you pay the fitting. The stainless steel drum is a free part for 3 years. Find the model and serial number, usually inside the door frame or on the back panel.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement motor if the motor in your LG washer dies. You pay only the labour after year one.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring LG on 1-800-243-0000 with your model number, serial number and receipt. Say you think the Direct Drive Motor has failed and ask for it to be booked under the 10-year motor warranty.
rules.script_hint: The Direct Drive Motor on my LG washer has failed and it is still inside the 10-year parts warranty, so the motor itself should come at no cost to me.

rules.title: HP laptop battery or power cord recall - free replacement, no time limit
rules.window_note: Safety recalls do not expire. HP still lists these programs today, and they cover laptops sold as far back as 2014. If yours was never swapped, you can still claim.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery (or a free replacement AC power cord) for HP and Compaq laptops on the recall list, because the originals can overheat and catch fire.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to HP's recalls page, open the battery program, and run HP's checker tool - it reads your battery's part number for you. If it is affected, HP ships a free replacement. Stop using the battery in the meantime.
rules.script_hint: HP's checker says my battery is affected by your safety recall, so I need the free replacement battery sent out.

rules.title: Whirlpool, Maytag, KitchenAid, Jenn-Air or Amana appliance recalls - free fix
rules.window_note: Recalls have no cut-off date. If your appliance was recalled and never fixed, the free fix is still owed to you years later. You need the model number and the serial number - they are on a sticker inside the door frame or behind a drawer.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, free replacement part, or a replacement appliance, depending on what the recall notice says. Whirlpool Corporation owns all these brands and lists its recalls in one place.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the model and serial number sticker on your appliance, then check it against Whirlpool Corporation's recall list. Each recall notice tells you the exact phone line or web form for that specific product.
rules.script_hint: My model and serial number match one of your recalls, and the fix was never done on my unit, so I would like the free remedy arranged.

rules.title: Car, tyre, car seat or trailer recall - free repair for 15 years
rules.window_note: US law makes the maker fix a safety recall for free for 15 years from the day the vehicle or the part was first bought new. For tyres it is 5 years. There is no charge and you do not need to have bought it new yourself.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair at a dealer for any open safety recall on your vehicle. Sometimes the maker replaces the part, refunds you, or buys the vehicle back instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Type your 17-character VIN into the recall checker at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If an open recall shows up, ring any franchised dealer for that brand and book the recall work. Say the word 'recall' - it is not a normal service booking.
rules.script_hint: My VIN shows an open safety recall, and I would like it booked in for the free recall repair.

rules.title: Check any Canadian product for a recall - free fix or refund
rules.window_note: Recalls have no expiry date. If your item was recalled and never dealt with, you can still claim. The database is updated every day and holds thousands of active alerts, so it's worth re-checking. Match the model number on your product to the one in the notice You can also sign up for email alerts.
rules.what_you_get: Whatever the recall notice offers - usually a free repair, a free replacement, or a refund from the maker.
rules.how_to_claim: Search recalls-rappels.canada.ca by brand name or product type. It covers Health Canada, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency and Transport Canada in one place. Then follow the instructions in the notice, or ring the company listed on it.
rules.script_hint: My product matches your recall notice and it was never fixed, so I would like the free remedy you promised in that notice.

rules.title: Check any UK product for a recall - free replacement, repair or refund
rules.window_note: There is no time limit on a recall. Old recalls stay claimable, and the government keeps a searchable list you can check any time. New alerts are added regularly, so search again whenever something goes wrong. You can filter by product type and by whether it's an alert, a report or a recall.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement, a free repair, or a refund from the maker or the shop - whichever the recall notice says.
rules.how_to_claim: Search the Product Safety Alerts, Reports and Recalls list on gov.uk for your brand and model. You can also sign up for email alerts. Then contact whoever the notice names.
rules.script_hint: My product is on the OPSS recall list and I have never had it dealt with, so I would like the free repair or replacement.

rules.title: Before you pay for any repair, search the maker's own 'service program' list
rules.window_note: These lists change all the time - programs get added and quietly retired. Check on the day your thing breaks, and check again if you get told no.
rules.what_you_get: Big makers quietly fix known faults for free long after the warranty ends, but they rarely tell you. Apple, Google, LG, Samsung, HP and Whirlpool all publish these lists on their own support sites.
rules.how_to_claim: Search the web for your brand plus the words 'service program' or 'extended repair program' plus your exact model and the fault, for example 'Pixel 8 extended repair program display line'. Only trust pages on the maker's own website. Then put in your serial number or IMEI on that page.
rules.script_hint: You publish a service program covering exactly this fault on this model, and my serial number qualifies, so I am asking for the free repair rather than a paid one.

rules.title: Bosch e-bike battery that lost most of its range
rules.window_note: Bosch's North American warranty runs 1 year from the day you bought it, and never past 60 months from when the battery was made. The capacity promise is tied to 500 full charges. Terms differ outside North America — check the sheet that came with your bike.
rules.what_you_get: If a Bosch e-bike battery has fallen below the capacity Bosch promises, Bosch replaces it free. In North America Bosch promises most sizes (400–800Wh) keep at least 60% of their capacity, and 300Wh batteries at least 70%, within 500 full charges.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the bike to the shop you bought it from with your dated receipt and ask them to plug it into the Bosch diagnostic tool and check the battery's real capacity against the guaranteed figure.
rules.script_hint: My range has collapsed. Can you run the Bosch diagnostic and check the battery's remaining capacity against Bosch's guaranteed capacity? I think it qualifies for a warranty replacement.

rules.title: Rad Power e-bike — 2 years on frame and battery
rules.window_note: 2 years from the day the bike reached you for the frame, forks, stem, bars, brakes, lights, rims, hubs and reflectors. The battery ends at 2 years OR 300 recharges, whichever comes first. Pedals, cranks, cassette, derailleur, shifter and saddle: 1 year. Tyres, tubes, brake pads, cables, grips, chain and spokes: never covered.
rules.what_you_get: Rad Power sends you a free replacement part — including a whole new battery or frame — when something fails from a build fault inside the window.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a case with Rad's Help Centre on their site. Take clear photos or a video of the fault first — they ask for these before they will ship anything.
rules.script_hint: My Rad Power [part] failed and the bike is under 2 years old. Here are photos and my order number — please send a warranty replacement.

rules.title: Segway scooter — battery only covered 180 days, so move fast
rules.window_note: Body of the scooter (deck, forks, stem, front hub motor, control board, dashboard, bars, charge port): 1 year. Battery pack and charger: only 180 days. Grips, fenders, lights, kickstand, grip tape: 90 days. Check the warranty sheet in your box — Segway varies this by model.
rules.what_you_get: Segway repairs or replaces the faulty part free, with new or refurbished parts, and pays the shipping back to you. The battery and charger window is short, so a battery that won't charge is worth reporting the same week it happens.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Segway on 1-866-473-4929 or email technicalsupport@segway.com with your serial number (on the underside of the deck, or in the Segway-Ninebot app) and your receipt. They give you an RMA number and you post the scooter in within 30 days.
rules.script_hint: My Segway scooter's battery won't charge. Here's the serial number and my receipt — please issue an RMA under the limited warranty.

rules.title: Car seat that was in a crash — get the letter, claim on insurance
rules.window_note: Do this while the crash claim is still open — insurers won't reopen a closed claim for it. NHTSA counts a crash as 'minor' (seat probably still fine) only if ALL of these are true: the car drove away, the door next to the seat wasn't damaged, nobody in the car was hurt, no airbags went off, and the seat has no visible damage. Anything worse and the seat has to go.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement car seat paid for by the car insurance claim, not by you. The seat's maker will send you a letter on their own letterhead saying the seat must be replaced after a crash — that letter is what the insurer wants before they pay.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the car seat's maker, give them the model and serial number off the sticker, and ask for their accident replacement policy letter. Send that letter and the receipt for the new seat to whoever is handling the crash claim.
rules.script_hint: My car seat was in a crash. Please email me your accident replacement policy letter with my model and serial number on it, so I can give it to my insurance company.

rules.title: UPPAbaby car seat covered for its whole life, stroller for 3 years
rules.window_note: Car seats: the whole usable life of the seat, up to 10 years from the date it was made (that date is printed on a sticker on the seat). Strollers: 3 years from the day you bought it — longer than most rivals give. Neither passes on if you sell it.
rules.what_you_get: UPPAbaby repairs the fault or sends you the replacement part free when a car seat or stroller has a manufacturing defect.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact UPPAbaby through their website with your receipt from an authorised UPPAbaby shop, plus the serial number and manufacture date from the sticker on the frame or seat shell.
rules.script_hint: My UPPAbaby [seat/stroller] has this fault. Here's my receipt and the serial number — please repair it or send the replacement part under warranty.

rules.title: Bugaboo pram — 4 years if you registered it
rules.window_note: 2 years as standard. Register within 3 months of buying and you get 2 extra years — 4 in total. Bought straight from bugaboo.com? You were registered automatically. Refurbished and outlet items don't get the extension, and outlet items only get 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: Bugaboo repairs or replaces a faulty chassis, seat frame, plastic seat part, wheel, adapter, zip, harness part or seam — free, and they cover the shipping both ways.
rules.how_to_claim: File a warranty claim on Bugaboo's site. You need a copy of your dated receipt, a clear description of what's wrong, and photos of the broken part.
rules.script_hint: My Bugaboo [part] has broken. It's registered so I'm on the extended 4-year warranty — here are photos and my receipt, please repair or replace it.

rules.title: UK: the shop must repair or replace it for free, and pay the postage
rules.window_note: There is no fixed cut-off. It lasts as long as you could still take the shop to court - six years in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, five in Scotland. But the older the item, the more you have to show the fault was there from the start.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or a free replacement. The shop has to cover parts, labour and postage, and get it done in a reasonable time without messing you around.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the shop that sold it - not the manufacturer. Your contract is with the shop, so 'it's out of warranty, call the maker' is not an answer they are allowed to give. Say whether you want a repair or a replacement.
rules.script_hint: Under section 23 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 I am asking you to repair or replace this at no cost to me, including labour and postage. My contract is with you, not the manufacturer.

rules.title: UK: in the first 6 months the shop has to prove it, not you
rules.window_note: Six months from the day it was delivered. This one does not apply to the 30-day full-refund right - only to repair, replacement, price reduction and the final right to hand it back. After six months you can still claim, but then it's on you to show the fault was there from the start. If they refuse and you paid by credit card, forward the very same email to your card company as a Section 75 claim.
rules.what_you_get: You do not have to prove anything. If it breaks in the first six months the law assumes the fault was already there when you got it, and the shop has to prove otherwise if it wants to refuse.
rules.how_to_claim: If the shop says 'you must have damaged it' or asks you to pay for an inspection report, point at this rule. The burden is on them, and paying for a report is not something you have to do.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: It failed within six months, so under section 19(14) of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 it is taken to have been faulty on the day it was delivered. If you disagree, it is for you to prove that, not me.

rules.title: EU: the manufacturer has to repair it even after the guarantee runs out
rules.window_note: Applies from 31 July 2026. It covers the products the EU has set repairability rules for - fridges and phones are named examples, and the list is set by EU ecodesign law rather than by how old your item is.
rules.what_you_get: A repair from the maker itself, free or at a fair price, done in a reasonable time - even years after any guarantee has ended. They are not allowed to use contract terms, hardware locks or software tricks to block the repair.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the manufacturer directly, not the shop, and ask for a repair under the EU repair obligation. Ask them for a European Repair Information Form first - it is a standard form with the price and timing on it, and once they give it to you the price is held for 30 days so you can shop around.
rules.script_hint: I am asking you to repair this under the EU Right to Repair Directive. Please send me a European Repair Information Form with the price and how long it will take.

rules.title: EU: if the maker advertised a long guarantee, go straight to the maker
rules.window_note: Lasts as long as the guarantee the maker advertised. This one only bites where the maker promised more than the standard two years - a '10 year guarantee' sticker, a lifetime promise on the box, a durability claim in the advert.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement from the manufacturer directly. You do not have to go back through the shop, and you do not have to argue about who is responsible.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the advertised promise - the box, the advert, the product page, the guarantee leaflet. Screenshot it. Then contact the manufacturer, not the shop, and ask them to honour it.
rules.script_hint: You advertise a durability guarantee on this product. Under Article 17 of the EU Sale of Goods Directive you are directly liable to me for repair or replacement for that whole period.

rules.title: France: two years of no-proof-needed, plus 12 months for choosing a repair
rules.window_note: Two years from delivery for new, refurbished and second-hand goods alike. For new goods you get the full 24 months of not having to prove anything; for second-hand and refurbished it is 12 months.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement. If you pick the repair, your guarantee is extended by 12 months. If the seller insists on replacing it instead, a fresh two-year guarantee starts from the day you get the replacement.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the seller (not the maker) for the garantie legale de conformite, and say you are choosing the repair. Get the 12-month extension confirmed on paper.
rules.script_hint: Je fais jouer la garantie legale de conformite. Je choisis la reparation, ce qui prolonge ma garantie de 12 mois. (I am using the legal guarantee of conformity. I choose repair, which extends my guarantee by 12 months.)

rules.title: France: money knocked straight off your repair bill
rules.window_note: Nothing to do with when you bought the item. It is tied to the repair you are having done now, so an old out-of-warranty item still qualifies.
rules.what_you_get: A discount taken straight off the repair invoice, paid for by a government-backed repair fund. Covers electrical and electronic goods, clothes, household linen, shoes, furniture, sports and leisure gear, DIY and garden tools, and toys.
rules.how_to_claim: Book the repair with a repairer that carries the QualiRepar label (or the matching label for clothes or furniture). The discount is applied to your bill automatically - there is no form to fill in and no money to claim back afterwards.
rules.script_hint: Est-ce que vous etes labellise QualiRepar ? Je voudrais le bonus reparation deduit de la facture. (Are you QualiRepar labelled? I would like the repair bonus taken off the bill.)

rules.title: Ireland: six years to claim, and they cannot keep re-repairing the same fault
rules.window_note: Six years counted from the day you received the goods. In the first 30 days you can simply reject it for a full refund. In the first 12 months the business has to prove it was not faulty.
rules.what_you_get: A repair, a replacement, money off or your money back - for up to six years, well past any manufacturer warranty. And if the same fault keeps coming back, you can refuse another repair and demand a replacement or a refund instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the business that sold it to you - your contract is with them, not the manufacturer. Say how many times it has been fixed already if this is a repeat fault.
rules.script_hint: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2022 my contract is with you as the seller, and I can seek a remedy for up to six years. This fault has already been repaired once, so I am asking for a replacement or a refund instead.

rules.title: Quebec: the shop cannot tell you to go bother the manufacturer
rules.window_note: Applies the whole time the legal warranty applies. It is about who you are allowed to chase, not about how old the item is.
rules.what_you_get: You get to pick. You can chase the shop, the manufacturer, or both at the same time - and the shop is not allowed to bounce you to the manufacturer's helpline instead of dealing with you.
rules.how_to_claim: If a store says 'that's a manufacturer issue, call them', say no and quote this rule. Then keep dealing with the store. Chasing both at once is allowed and often faster.
rules.script_hint: Quebec's consumer protection office says a merchant may not require me to deal with the manufacturer. I am claiming the legal warranty from you, the merchant.

rules.title: Quebec: fixed free-repair years per appliance, starting 5 October 2026
rules.window_note: Starts 5 October 2026 - not claimable before that date. Then the clock runs from delivery: 6 years for fridges, freezers, stoves, air conditioners and heat pumps; 5 years for washers, dryers and dishwashers; 4 years for televisions; 3 years for desktops, laptops, tablets, phones and games consoles.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair with no argument about what 'reasonable' means. Parts, labour and reasonable shipping are all covered by the merchant or the manufacturer.
rules.how_to_claim: From 5 October 2026, contact the merchant or the manufacturer, say which category your item falls in and how long you have had it, and ask for the free repair under the warranty of good working order.
rules.script_hint: This is covered by Quebec's warranty of good working order. My item is inside the set period for its category, so you are required to repair it free of charge, including parts and labour.

rules.title: Quebec: no parts, no repair service? Then they replace it or refund you
rules.window_note: Starts 5 October 2026 - not claimable before that date. It covers anything that needs maintenance, from a toaster to a car.
rules.what_you_get: Spare parts, a repair service, and the information needed to fix it - all at prices that are not set high enough to put you off repairing. Repair information posted on the maker's own platform has to be free. If they cannot deliver, you can demand a replacement or your money back instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the merchant or manufacturer in writing to repair the item. From that request they have 10 days to come back with a written repair proposal. If they do not reply, or they miss their own promised repair deadline, you can then demand a replacement or a refund.
rules.script_hint: I am asking you to repair this under Quebec's warranty of availability of parts and repair services. You have 10 days to send me a written repair proposal, or I will be asking for a replacement or a refund.

rules.title: BC, Saskatchewan and New Brunswick: goods must be durable, by law
rules.window_note: No fixed number of years - the test is what is reasonable for that kind of product used that way. Each province has its own court deadline for actually suing, so do not sit on it. In New Brunswick you can claim even if you were not the person who bought it - a gift counts. Every province also has a deadline for going to court — usually around two years from when you noticed the problem Applies to items bought or leased from a business, not from a private seller.
rules.what_you_get: A built-in promise, attached to every sale, that the item and its parts will last a reasonable period of time. It cannot be signed away, and 'sold as is, no warranty' does not remove it in a normal consumer sale.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the retailer. Say what you paid, how long it lasted, and that the province's statutory durability warranty applies regardless of the manufacturer's warranty. If they refuse, small claims court is the backstop.
rules.script_hint: The law in this province gives an implied warranty that goods will be durable for a reasonable period of time. This item was not. That warranty applies whatever the manufacturer's warranty says, and it cannot be waived.

rules.title: Saskatchewan: spare parts and repair shops must actually be available
rules.window_note: Runs for a reasonable period after you bought it - no fixed number of years. It only applies to products that normally need servicing or repair.
rules.what_you_get: A promise, built into the sale, that spare parts and somewhere to get it repaired will exist for a reasonable time after you buy. If the maker discontinued the part a year in, that is a breach you can push on.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Saskatchewan's Consumer Protection Division for guidance, then put your complaint to the retailer or manufacturer in writing. These statutory warranties cannot be excluded, and trying to exclude them can itself be an offence.
rules.script_hint: Saskatchewan's statutory warranties say spare parts and repair facilities must be available for a reasonable period after purchase. They are not, so I am asking you to repair, replace or refund this.

rules.title: Visa Signature / Visa Infinite: one extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Kicks in the day the maker's warranty runs out. Only works if that warranty was 3 years or less, so the latest it can help you is about 4 years after you bought the thing. The clock that really matters is after it breaks: call within 60 days or they can say no. Once the item breaks you have only 60 days to phone, and 90 days to send the paperwork. Banks pick which Visa benefits to switch on, so check your own card's Guide to Benefits before you count on it.
rules.what_you_get: Your Visa card quietly adds a whole extra year onto the maker's warranty. So if your TV died 14 months in and the maker only covered 12 months, Visa can pay to fix it, or replace it, or pay you back what you spent - up to $10,000 for that one item and $50,000 total.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Visa Benefit Administrator at 1-888-221-3289 as soon as the item stops working. Have ready: the receipt, the card statement showing you paid with the Visa, and the maker's warranty paper. They send you a claim form and tell you which repair shop to use.
rules.script_hint: I have a Visa Signature card and I'm filing an Extended Warranty Protection claim. I bought this on my card, the manufacturer's warranty was under three years, it just failed, and I'm calling within sixty days of the failure.

rules.title: Standard Mastercard: doubles a one-year warranty
rules.window_note: Only helps if the maker's warranty was 12 months or less. It doubles that, so most people are covered until roughly two years after they bought it. After it breaks you get 60 days to report it and 180 days to send the paperwork. On World and World Elite cards it works on warranties up to 24 months and adds up to 24 months. If the maker's warranty is longer than that limit, you get nothing. The maker's warranty and a repair estimate from an authorised shop.
rules.what_you_get: A basic Mastercard doubles the maker's warranty by up to 12 extra months. Most electronics come with one year, so this usually gets you a second year free. They pay the repair or replacement, capped at what you charged to the card or $10,000, whichever is smaller.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-627-8372 (that's 1-800-Mastercard) or go to mycardbenefits.com and start a claim within 60 days of the day it broke. Then send in the receipt and the card statement showing the purchase within 180 days.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open a Mastercard Extended Warranty claim. I paid for this entirely with my Mastercard, it came with a manufacturer's warranty of twelve months or less, and it failed on this date - within the last sixty days.

rules.title: World Elite Mastercard: up to two extra years of warranty
rules.window_note: Works on maker's warranties of 24 months or less, and doubles them - so a 2-year warranty becomes 4 years. Report the failure within 60 days and get your paperwork in within 180 days of the failure.
rules.what_you_get: A World or World Elite Mastercard doubles the maker's warranty by up to 24 extra months - twice as much as a plain Mastercard. They repair it, replace it, or pay you back what you charged, up to $10,000.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call the number in your card's Guide to Benefits (Capital One World Elite cardholders use 1-877-288-6784) within 60 days of the day it broke. Send the receipt, your statement and the warranty paper within 180 days.
rules.script_hint: I have a World Elite Mastercard and I'm opening an Extended Warranty claim. The manufacturer's warranty was twenty-four months or less, the item failed on this date, and I'm reporting inside sixty days.

rules.title: World Elite Mastercard: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Nothing to do with when you bought the phone. You are covered from the first day of the month after you pay a phone bill with the card, and you stay covered every month you keep paying that bill with it. Report a break or theft within 90 days, and send proof within 120 days.
rules.what_you_get: If you pay your monthly phone bill with the card, a smashed or stolen phone gets fixed or replaced - up to $800 per claim, minus a $50 deductible, and up to 2 claims in 12 months. Covers every phone line on that bill, not just yours.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call 1-877-288-6784 within 90 days of the damage or theft. You'll need the card statement showing you paid last month's phone bill with the card, plus a police report if it was stolen.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a Cellular Wireless Telephone Protection claim on my World Elite Mastercard. I pay my monthly wireless bill with this card and my phone was stolen/damaged on this date.

rules.title: Citi: two extra years of warranty
rules.window_note: Citi adds 24 months on top of the maker's warranty, with total cover capped at 7 years from the day you bought it. Send all requested documents within 180 days of the failure. Careful: Citi stripped these benefits from a lot of its cards, so check yours first.
rules.what_you_get: On the Citi cards that still have it, Citi adds a full 24 months to the maker's warranty - double what most cards give. They repair, replace or pay you back up to $10,000 per item.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-866-506-5222 (8am to midnight ET, any day) or go to mybenefits.cardbenefitclaims.com as soon as the item fails. First, check your card actually has the benefit - look up your card's Guide to Protection Benefits at cardbenefits.citi.com.
rules.script_hint: I want to open an Extended Warranty claim on my Citi card. Can you confirm my card has this benefit? The item failed on this date and the manufacturer's warranty has run out.

rules.title: Citi extended warranty (US)
rules.window_note: Citi adds up to 24 extra months, with total cover capped at 7 years from the purchase date. Worth checking even if you were told years ago that Citi had dropped it: Citi cut most of these benefits on 22 September 2019, then added a 2-year extended warranty back to cards like Double Cash and Custom Cash from 17 November 2024. Send documents within 180 days of the failure.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement after the maker's warranty ends, up to $10,000 per item.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to cardbenefits.citi.com or call 1-866-918-4670 as soon as the item stops working, and return every document they ask for within 180 days of the breakdown. Check your own card's Guide to Protection Benefits first, because not every Citi card has this.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to file a Citi Extended Warranty claim. My [item] failed after the manufacturer's warranty ran out, and I paid for it in full with this Citi card.

rules.title: Citi: damaged or stolen in the first 90 days
rules.window_note: Covers the first 90 days from purchase or delivery, whichever comes first. Get your documents in within 180 days of the incident. Citi removed this from many cards, so confirm yours has it.
rules.what_you_get: Citi's Damage and Theft Purchase Protection repairs or pays back an item damaged or stolen in its first 90 days - up to $10,000 per incident and $50,000 a year. It even covers the deductible on your home insurance.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-866-506-5222 or go to mybenefits.cardbenefitclaims.com as soon as it happens. Have the receipt, the statement, and a police report for theft.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a Damage and Theft Purchase Protection claim on my Citi card. I bought this within the last ninety days and it was damaged/stolen on this date.

rules.title: Citi: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Not tied to when you bought the phone - it's tied to paying your monthly phone bill with the Citi card. Report within 90 days of the break or theft, and send written proof within 120 days.
rules.what_you_get: If your monthly phone bill goes on the Citi card, a damaged or stolen phone gets repaired or replaced. Covers the main line and extra lines on the same bill. Cracked screens that don't stop the phone working are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-833-763-6324 (Mon-Fri, 8am to 8pm ET) or go to phonebenefit.com within 90 days of the damage or theft. Bring the statement showing last month's phone bill paid with the card, and a police report if stolen.
rules.script_hint: I'm opening a cell phone protection claim on my Citi card. I pay my wireless bill with this card and my phone was damaged/stolen on this date, within the last ninety days.

rules.title: Capital One: still has extended warranty in 2026
rules.window_note: How long the extension runs depends on your card's network. World Elite Mastercard versions add up to 24 months; Visa versions add 12. Capital One says to file within 60 to 90 days of the thing breaking.
rules.what_you_get: Capital One kept this benefit while others dropped it. Venture, VentureOne, Savor, SavorOne, Quicksilver and QuicksilverOne all have extended warranty. Covers TVs, phones and appliances that aren't wired or plumbed in - so a toaster yes, a built-in dishwasher no.
rules.how_to_claim: Mastercard versions: call 800-627-8372 or go to mycardbenefits.com. Visa and Discover versions: call 844-288-2140 or go to cardbenefitservices.com. File within 60 days of the failure to be safe. Bring the itemised receipt, the maker's warranty, a repair estimate and the statement showing the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an extended warranty claim on my Capital One card. The item failed after the manufacturer's warranty ended and I bought it with this card.

rules.title: Capital One Venture X adds a free extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Only works if the maker's warranty was 3 years or shorter. It adds 1 more year on top. Call within 60 days of the item breaking and send the signed form within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim and $50,000 per cardholder.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140 right after the item fails. Have the receipt, warranty paper, and card statement.
rules.script_hint: The maker's warranty just ended and my item stopped working. I bought it on my Capital One Venture X and want an extended warranty claim.

rules.title: Capital One Visa Signature cards add a free extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Covers Capital One Visa Signature cards like Venture, VentureOne, Savor and Quicksilver. Only works on maker warranties of 3 years or less. Call within 60 days of the breakdown and send the form within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim and $50,000 per cardholder. These cards do not have cell phone or return protection.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140. You can also register the warranty ahead of time by calling the same number.
rules.script_hint: My item's maker warranty just ran out and it failed. I bought it on my Capital One Visa Signature card and want an extended warranty claim.

rules.title: Capital One World Elite Mastercard doubles your warranty, up to 2 extra years
rules.window_note: Works on maker or store warranties of 24 months or less and doubles them, so a 2-year warranty becomes 4 years. Report within 60 days of the breakdown and send written proof within 180 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim. Their damage and theft cover is separate and smaller: $1,000 per loss within 90 days of buying.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call 1-800-627-8372. Have the receipt, warranty paper, and card statement.
rules.script_hint: My item's warranty just ran out and it stopped working. I bought it on my Capital One World Elite Mastercard and want an extended warranty claim.

rules.title: Wells Fargo: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Nothing to do with when you bought the phone. Cover starts on the first day of the month after your phone bill posts to the Wells Fargo card, and stops if you skip a month. Report within 60 days of the loss. Send documents within 120 days. Lost phones are not covered.
rules.what_you_get: Pay your monthly phone bill with a Wells Fargo card and a damaged, stolen or accidentally-lost-forever phone gets fixed or replaced - up to $600 a claim minus a $25 deductible, 2 paid claims and $1,200 max in 12 months. Every line on that bill is covered. Cracked screens that don't affect how it works are not.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-316-8051 or go to mycardbenefits.assurant.com within 60 days of the damage or theft. You'll need the wireless bill showing the whole monthly payment went on the Wells Fargo card.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a Cellular Telephone Protection claim on my Wells Fargo card. I paid my full wireless bill with this card last month and my phone was damaged/stolen on this date.

rules.title: Wells Fargo: one extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Works on maker's warranties of 36 months or less and adds 12 months, so a 3-year warranty becomes 4 years. If the maker's warranty is longer than 36 months you get nothing extra. Report within 60 days of the failure.
rules.what_you_get: Wells Fargo adds 12 months onto the maker's warranty when you paid for the whole thing with the card. They cover the repair or a like-for-like replacement, up to $10,000 an item and $50,000 in a year.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-316-8051 or go to mycardbenefits.assurant.com within 60 days of the item failing. You can also upload your receipt and warranty to that site right after you buy something so it's ready later.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an Extended Warranty Protection claim on my Wells Fargo card. I paid for the item in full with this card, the manufacturer's warranty was thirty-six months or less, and it failed on this date.

rules.title: U.S. Bank Visa Platinum: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: You must have charged your monthly phone bill to the U.S. Bank Visa Platinum in the calendar month before the phone broke or was stolen. Report it quickly - these benefits usually allow 60 to 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $600 per claim, minus a $25 deductible, and $1,200 or 2 claims in a 12-month period. Covers damage, theft, and a phone that's accidentally gone for good. Does NOT cover a phone you simply lost, or one that just stopped working on its own.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to usbank.com/cellphoneprotection or call the number on the back of your card and ask for the cell phone protection benefit administrator. Bring the statement showing last month's phone bill on the card, and a police report if it was stolen.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a cell phone protection claim on my U.S. Bank Visa Platinum. I charged my monthly cell phone bill to this card the month before my phone was damaged/stolen.

rules.title: The 60-day rule that kills most card claims
rules.window_note: This is the deadline nobody knows about. Visa, Mastercard and Wells Fargo give you 60 days from the day the item breaks. American Express gives you only 30. Chase gives 90. The warranty itself might have years left - but if you sit on it, the card benefit is gone.
rules.what_you_get: Knowing this is worth money. People assume a card's extended warranty lasts as long as the coverage does. It doesn't - the moment the thing breaks, a short clock starts, and once it runs out the claim is dead no matter how good your case is.
rules.how_to_claim: The day something you bought on a credit card breaks or gets stolen, phone the card's benefit administrator - the number is on the back of your card. Open the claim first, gather paperwork after. Opening the claim is what stops the clock.
rules.script_hint: I want to open a claim today to protect my deadline, even though I don't have all my paperwork yet. Please note the date I reported this.

rules.title: A written warranty means nobody can erase your basic "it has to work" right
rules.window_note: In most states you get about 4 years from the day the item was handed to you, which is often much longer than the printed warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A second, quieter promise on top of the printed warranty: the thing has to actually work for what it's normally used for. If the product came with any written warranty at all, or you bought an extended service plan within 90 days, nobody is allowed to take that promise away in the fine print.
rules.how_to_claim: When the maker says "sorry, out of warranty" but the thing died far too soon, write to the store you bought it from and say the item was never fit to use. Ask for a refund or replacement. Small claims court is the backstop and you don't need a lawyer there.
rules.script_hint: This came with a written warranty, so under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act the implied warranty can't be disclaimed. This product didn't work the way this kind of product normally should.

rules.title: Stuff has to actually work — for about 4 years you can hold the store to it
rules.window_note: Almost every state gives you 4 years from the day the item was delivered to you. A handful of contracts legally shorten it to 1 year, so read the receipt. The clock starts at delivery, not at the day it broke. It does not cover damage from misuse, accidents, or normal wear.
rules.what_you_get: A repair, replacement or refund from the store even when there is no warranty paper at all, because the law says goods sold by a business have to be fit for the job they're sold for. It also covers used items when you bought them from a business.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the store, not the maker. Put it in writing: what you bought, when, what it failed to do, and what you want. If they say no, small claims court is cheap, fast and lawyer-free.
rules.script_hint: This wasn't fit for the ordinary purpose it's sold for, so the store has broken the implied warranty of merchantability. I'd like a refund or a replacement.

rules.title: Five states don't let anyone sell you a dud "as is"
rules.window_note: Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, West Virginia and Kansas only. Same rough 4-year clock from the day you got it. Works on clearance items, floor models and used things bought from a business.
rules.what_you_get: In these five states, "sold as is" and "no warranty" fine print simply doesn't work on consumer goods — a court will ignore it. The basic promise that the thing works stays with you no matter what the receipt says. In Kansas a judge can also make them pay your lawyer.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the store, not the maker. Tell them your state does not allow them to disclaim the implied warranty, and name your state's law. Keep the receipt and any photo of the "as is" sign.
rules.script_hint: "As is" isn't enforceable here — my state bans it on consumer goods (MA c.106 s.2-316A, MD Com. Law 2-316.1, ME 11 s.2-316(5), WV 46A-6-107, KS 50-639). The implied warranty still applies, so I'd like a refund.

rules.title: If your warranty says FULL, repeated failures mean refund or replacement
rules.window_note: Only while the full warranty runs. Look at the top of your warranty paper — it has to say "Full" (like "Full One-Year Warranty"). If it says "Limited", this one doesn't apply to you. Write to them, list the dates of every failed repair, and say you are choosing a refund (or a replacement) because it's your choice under the law.
rules.what_you_get: After the company has had a fair number of tries and still can't fix it, you choose: your money back, or a brand new one. Free. They also can't charge you for the repair itself, and the only thing they're allowed to ask of you is that you tell them it's broken.
rules.how_to_claim: Count your repair attempts and find the dates. Call the warranty line, say how many times it has been in, and ask for the refund-or-replace choice in writing.
rules.script_hint: This is a Full warranty, so under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, after a reasonable number of failed repairs I get to choose a refund or a free replacement. I'm choosing a refund.

rules.title: A FULL warranty follows the product, not the first buyer
rules.window_note: Only while the original Full warranty is still running, counted from when it was first sold new — not from when you bought it secondhand.
rules.what_you_get: If you bought it used and there is time left on a Full warranty, the free repair is yours too. You don't need to be the person whose name is on the original receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the maker's warranty line, give the serial number, and ask them to check warranty status by serial number. Serial number lookups are how they date the product without your receipt.
rules.script_hint: This has a Full warranty, and under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act a Full warranty covers whoever owns the product, not just the first buyer. Here's the serial number.

rules.title: Not mailing the registration card doesn't cost you the warranty
rules.window_note: Any time the warranty is still running. Strongest when the warranty says "Full" — that's exactly what the FTC rule covers.
rules.what_you_get: Your warranty still counts even though you binned the little card or never registered online. They can ask for the card as proof of when you bought it, but they can't make it a condition of fixing your stuff.
rules.how_to_claim: Claim as normal. If they say "you never registered", offer your receipt, bank statement or order email as proof of the purchase date instead, and point at the FTC rule.
rules.script_hint: The FTC's rule at 16 CFR 700.7 says making me return a registration card as a condition of warranty service is an unreasonable duty. Here's my receipt for the purchase date.

rules.title: California: the lemon law covers regular stuff, not just cars
rules.window_note: California only. Works while the written warranty is still running. Most people have never heard this applies to a fridge or a laptop, but it does. Ask the maker or the shop in writing for a repair under the Song-Beverly Act. If it ends up in court, you generally have about 4 years from the purchase date. Once it's past 30 days, or after two or three failed fixes, ask in writing for a replacement or a refund and attach your log. Warranty repairs have to be finished within 30 days, unless you agree in writing to wait longer.
rules.what_you_get: If the maker can't fix it after a fair number of tries, California law makes them replace it or hand back what you paid, minus a small amount for the use you already got out of it. Warranty repairs have to be finished within 30 days, unless you agree in writing to wait longer.
rules.how_to_claim: Keep every repair ticket — dates matter more than anything else here. Then write to the maker, not the store, list the dates it went in for the same fault, and ask for a replacement or a refund.
rules.script_hint: Under California Civil Code 1793.2(d)(1), after a reasonable number of repair attempts you have to replace this or refund me. Here are the repair dates.

rules.title: California: warranty repairs are supposed to be finished in 30 days
rules.window_note: California only. Applies to any repair being done under a written warranty. The clock can stretch if something outside the maker's control holds it up, like a genuine parts shortage.
rules.what_you_get: A deadline you can actually hold them to. If your stuff has been sitting at the repair centre past 30 days, that's a broken legal promise and it's your best lever for asking for a replacement instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Count the days from when you handed it over. Email the maker and the repair centre with the drop-off date in writing and ask for a completion date.
rules.script_hint: California Civil Code 1793.2(b) says warranty repairs must be finished within 30 days. It's been 45. When is it going back together, or are we talking about a replacement?

rules.title: California: your warranty clock pauses while the thing is in the shop
rules.window_note: California only. The pause starts the day you hand it over (or the day you tell them it's broken) and ends the day you get it back or they tell you it's ready.
rules.what_you_get: Free extra warranty days. Every day your product spends waiting for or getting a warranty repair does not count against your warranty — so a six-week repair pushes your expiry date six weeks later.
rules.how_to_claim: Keep the work order or receipt showing the drop-off date and the date you got it back. When the maker later says you're out of warranty, add those days back on and show them the paperwork.
rules.script_hint: California Civil Code 1795.6 pauses the warranty while the product is being repaired. You had it from March 3rd to April 20th, so my warranty runs 48 days longer than your system says.

rules.title: California: a hidden safety net that can run a full year
rules.window_note: California only, on new goods. Never shorter than 60 days and never longer than 1 year from the day you bought it — so a 90-day warranty doesn't mean you're bare on day 91. It matches the written warranty length in between.
rules.what_you_get: A basic "it has to work" promise that runs alongside the printed warranty and can last up to a year, even when the maker only gave you 30 or 90 days.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the store or the maker inside that year and say the item wasn't fit to use. Put it in writing. California small claims court is cheap and you're not allowed to bring a lawyer, so the company can't out-lawyer you.
rules.script_hint: California Civil Code 1791.1(c) gives me an implied warranty of up to one year on new consumer goods, so I'm still covered. This wasn't fit for normal use.

rules.title: New York: the maker must sell parts and manuals to your local shop
rules.window_note: New York only, and only for gear first made or sold in New York after 1 July 2023. Home appliances, power tools, cars, yard and garden equipment, farm gear and medical devices are all left out.
rules.what_you_get: A cheaper repair. You or any independent shop can buy the same parts and tools the maker's own authorised shops buy, at the same price, and the repair documents have to be free.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any independent repair shop, or ask the maker directly for the part and the manual. If they refuse or quote a silly price, file a complaint with the New York Attorney General's consumer bureau.
rules.script_hint: New York's Digital Fair Repair Act (General Business Law 399-nn) requires you to make this part and the repair documentation available to me on fair and reasonable terms.

rules.title: Minnesota: parts, tools and manuals within 60 days of a product's launch
rules.window_note: Minnesota only, for gear sold on or after 1 July 2021. Cars, medical devices, farm and construction gear, game consoles and home battery systems are left out. Minnesota's version covers appliances, which New York's does not. Including software updates needed for the repair.
rules.what_you_get: You or an independent shop can buy the parts and tools and get the repair documents on fair terms — and the maker has to have them ready within 60 days of the product first going on sale in Minnesota.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker, or have your repair shop ask, for the specific part, tool or manual. Keep any refusal in writing — refusing breaks Minnesota's deceptive trade practices law, so report it to the Minnesota Attorney General.
rules.script_hint: Minnesota Statute 325E.72 requires you to make this documentation, part or tool available to me on fair and reasonable terms. Please confirm in writing if you're refusing.

rules.title: Paid by credit card? The law lets you hand the fight to your card company
rules.window_note: Credit cards only — not debit, not cash. The law itself sets no hard deadline, but card companies get strict fast, so call within a couple of months of giving up on the seller. Normally the purchase has to be over $50 and made in your home state or within 100 miles of your address, though that limit drops away if the card company and the seller are connected.
rules.what_you_get: Your money back through your card company when a seller sold you something broken and won't put it right. This is stronger than a normal chargeback: you're raising the same complaint against the card company that you had against the shop.
rules.how_to_claim: First genuinely try the seller and keep proof that you tried — emails, chat logs, a call log. Then ring the number on the back of your card and use the exact wording below, because "claims and defenses" is routed differently inside the bank than a plain disputed charge.
rules.script_hint: I'm asserting my claims and defenses under the Fair Credit Billing Act, section 170. The merchant sold me a defective product and won't fix it, and I've made a good faith attempt to resolve it with them.

rules.title: Whirlpool or Maytag bottom-freezer fridge that ices up and leaks onto the floor
rules.window_note: The fridge has to be less than 5 years old when it ices up, and you need to report it within 90 days. The whole thing shuts on 31 December 2026.
rules.what_you_get: A free new drain tube part, and Whirlpool pays the repair bill: the whole thing in years 1 to 3, all the parts plus most of the labour in years 4 and 5.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring Whirlpool's special service line on 1-888-900-7957 and report it. A Whirlpool engineer has to see it, so book the visit through that number rather than calling your own repair person.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to report a Future Freezing Event under the Corzine v. Whirlpool settlement. Ice built up in my freezer, the drain froze, and water ran out onto my floor. My model is on the Group B list.

rules.title: Keurig K-Supreme coffee maker that died while you were descaling it
rules.window_note: You need to have owned the machine at some point between 1 October 2020 and 20 June 2025. If it lost power after 20 June 2025, you have until 30 September 2027 to ask.
rules.what_you_get: A 12-month extended warranty on your coffee maker, which means Keurig has to repair or replace it for free instead of you buying a new one.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the claim form at ksupremesettlement.com. Say your machine permanently lost power during descaling and that you want the extended warranty.
rules.script_hint: I own a K-Supreme and it permanently lost power while I was descaling it, following Keurig's own instructions. I'm in the Coffee Maker Purchaser Class in the Cahill v. Keurig settlement and I'm claiming the 12-month extended warranty.

rules.title: Toyota with the airbag control unit that could fail in a crash
rules.window_note: Covers 2011-2019 Corolla, 2011-2013 Corolla Matrix, 2012-2018 Avalon, 2013-2018 Avalon HV, 2012-2019 Tacoma, 2012-2017 Tundra and 2012-2017 Sequoia. You have until 11 December 2028, so this one is not urgent.
rules.what_you_get: Money back for what this cost you out of pocket, a cash payment, a free loaner car while the work is done, a free inspection, and a longer warranty on the new parts.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to airbagcontrolunitsettlement.com, put your VIN in the lookup tool, then submit the claim form online or by post.
rules.script_hint: I own a Toyota listed in the ZF-TRW airbag control unit settlement. I'd like to file a claim for my out-of-pocket costs and the extended parts warranty.

rules.title: Kia Optima or Sportage where a window won't roll up or down
rules.window_note: Covers certain 2016-2017 Kia Optima and all 2017 Kia Sportage cars. How much you get back depends on the mileage when the window broke, not on how long ago you bought it. Closes 23 November 2026.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $400 back for each window you paid to fix, up to four windows on one car. You get 100% back under 35,000 miles, sliding down to 40% over 125,000 miles. If you still own the car you can take a $40 dealer service card instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to kiawindowregulatorsettlement.com, check your VIN, then upload the repair invoice showing you paid for a window regulator replacement.
rules.script_hint: I paid out of pocket to replace a window regulator on my Kia, which is a class vehicle in the Le Beau v. Kia settlement. Here is my invoice and my mileage at the time.

rules.title: Honda or Acura whose engine won't restart after Auto Idle Stop
rules.window_note: Covers 2015-2020 Acura TLX, 2016-2020 Acura MDX, 2016-2021 Honda Pilot, 2019-2021 Honda Passport and 2020-2021 Honda Ridgeline. Free repairs run for 10 years from when the car was first sold new, with an extra 24 months for 2015 TLX and an extra 18 months for 2016 TLX, MDX and Pilot. Towing costs must be claimed within 60 days of paying them.
rules.what_you_get: A free starter replacement or valve adjustment at a Honda or Acura dealer. Because of this settlement the dealer is not allowed to make the fault happen in front of them first. Towing costs get paid back too.
rules.how_to_claim: Book your car into an authorised Honda or Acura dealer and ask for the Auto Idle Stop repair under the service bulletin. Do not let them turn you away for not being able to reproduce the fault.
rules.script_hint: My car is covered by the Honda Idle Stop settlement and it's still inside the 10-year warranty extension. Under that settlement you can't require me to reproduce the no-restart symptom before doing the free starter replacement.

rules.title: Subaru where the EyeSight auto-braking or lane-keeping stopped working
rules.window_note: Covers certain 2013-2024 Subarus with EyeSight. The extra cover runs for 4 years or 48,000 miles from the day the car went into service, whichever comes first. It moves with the car, so it still counts if you bought it used. Claims for repairs you already paid for closed on 27 September 2025 — this is only for repairs you get done now.
rules.what_you_get: Subaru pays 75% of the repair bill when the EyeSight camera or the rear sonar sensor makes the pre-collision braking, rear auto braking or lane-keep assist stop working.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your VIN on eyesightsettlement.com, then take the car to an authorised Subaru dealer and ask them to do the repair under the settlement's warranty extension.
rules.script_hint: My VIN is a class vehicle in the Subaru EyeSight settlement, and I'm still inside the 4-year, 48,000-mile warranty extension. Please book this repair under that extension so 75% is covered.

rules.title: VW Atlas or Atlas Cross Sport with a failed water pump
rules.window_note: Covers 2018-2022 Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport with the 3.6 litre engine. The extra cover runs 8.5 years or 85,000 miles from the day the car went into service. Claims for repairs you already paid for close on 5 October 2026.
rules.what_you_get: 80% of what a water pump repair costs. If you used a non-VW garage, the payout is capped at $820 for the water pump or $3,325 for a head gasket.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your VIN on the settlement website, then send the signed claim form with your repair invoices to the administrator so it's postmarked by 5 October 2026.
rules.script_hint: My VW Atlas has the 3.6 litre engine and is covered by the main engine water pump settlement. I paid out of pocket for a water pump repair and I'm claiming the 80% reimbursement.

rules.title: Bestway, Power Steel, Steel Pro or Coleman above-ground pool (48 inches or taller)
rules.window_note: Covers pools sold from 2008 through 2024 that are 48 inches tall or more with the straps running on the outside of the legs. No time limit from when you bought it, but everything closes on 30 October 2026.
rules.what_you_get: $40 in cash with no receipt at all, or 10% of what you actually paid if you still have the receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the claim form at poolsettlementbw.com. You don't need a receipt for the $40 — you just sign to say you bought one.
rules.script_hint: I bought a Bestway above-ground pool that's 48 inches or taller with the compression straps on the outside of the legs. I'm filing a claim without proof of purchase.

rules.title: Sanyo solar panels on your house that are peeling apart
rules.window_note: Covers Sanyo HIP-xxxBA2, BA3 and BA5 panels sold for homes, roughly 2001 to 2010. You have until 20 years after they were bought, or 31 December 2029, whichever comes first. It counts even if the panels came with the house when you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: A free new or refurbished panel to replace each bad one, or cash based on what the panel originally cost minus wear. A panel bought 10 years ago for $700 pays about $350.
rules.how_to_claim: Take clear photos of the peeling, then email the claim form, photos and proof you own the panels to sanyosolarclaims@4class.com. The form is on sanyosolarclaims.com.
rules.script_hint: I own Sanyo HIP-series solar panels that are delaminating. I'm filing a claim under the Ziccarello v. Sanyo settlement, with photos of the circular delamination.

rules.title: CertainTeed Horizon roof shingles that are failing
rules.window_note: Covers buildings in the US where CertainTeed Fiberglass Horizon shingles were put on between 1995 and 2010. You have until 2 March 2030, so there's no rush.
rules.what_you_get: A cash payment if your roof shingles show the kind of damage the settlement covers.
rules.how_to_claim: Start the claim at ctroof.com, or post the claim form to the Horizon Settlement Administrator, 805 W. 5th Street, Suite 7, Lansdale, PA 19446. You'll need to show the damage.
rules.script_hint: My building has CertainTeed Fiberglass Horizon shingles installed between 1995 and 2010, and they're showing qualifying damage. I'm filing a claim under the Segebarth v. CertainTeed settlement.

rules.title: Pixel Care+ pays $0 for a battery under 80%
rules.window_note: While your Pixel Care+ cover is running. Plans are sold as a 2 year term or month by month.
rules.what_you_get: A new battery at zero cost if yours holds less than 80% of its original charge. Screens and back glass are $0 on the same plan.
rules.how_to_claim: Check Pixel battery health in Settings, then Battery. Google says a Pixel 8a or later should still hold 80% at around 1000 charges, and a Pixel 3 to 8 Pro at around 800 charges. If you are under 80% and you have Pixel Care+, start a repair through Google Store support and say it is a Pixel Care+ battery claim. Without Pixel Care+, the plain warranty only pays out for a battery that is actually defective, not one that has simply aged.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel battery holds less than 80% of its original capacity and I have Pixel Care+, so this should be a $0 battery replacement.

rules.title: Milwaukee tools get 5 years, the batteries only get about 3
rules.window_note: Most M12 and M18 REDLITHIUM packs are 3 years from purchase, a few older packs are only 2. The tool itself is usually 5 years, and Milwaukee hand tools are lifetime. If you have no receipt they can read the manufacturing date printed on the pack. You do not have to register the tool first.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery pack if it fails inside the battery's own shorter window.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the pack's catalogue number printed on the battery (like 48-11-1862) and look it up on Milwaukee's warranty page to get its exact years. Then take the pack and your receipt to a Milwaukee authorised service centre. Do not assume the tool's 5 years covers it.
rules.script_hint: I know the battery pack has its own warranty length, separate from the tool. Can you check the coverage on catalogue number [number]?

rules.title: DeWalt 20V MAX battery packs carry 3 years
rules.window_note: 3 years from purchase or delivery, whichever is later. There is also a 90 day money back window if you simply are not happy with it.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of a battery pack that failed from faulty materials or workmanship.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the pack and proof of purchase to a DeWalt factory service centre or authorised service centre. Say it is a 3 year limited warranty claim. If you are still inside 90 days and just unhappy with the runtime, ask for the money back guarantee instead, which is easier to win.
rules.script_hint: This battery is under three years old and it has failed. I'm claiming under the 3 Year Limited Warranty.

rules.title: Ryobi gives batteries 3 years but accessories only 90 days
rules.window_note: 3 years from purchase for tools and for batteries. Accessories are only 90 days, so claim those fast.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a tool or battery with a workmanship or materials fault.
rules.how_to_claim: Register or find your proof of purchase, then contact Ryobi support or take it to an authorised service centre. Ask them to confirm which bucket your item falls in, because a battery gets 3 years while a blade or attachment may only get 90 days.
rules.script_hint: This is a Ryobi battery, which carries the three year warranty, not the ninety day accessory warranty.

rules.title: Toyota hybrid batteries get 10 years, and it follows the car
rules.window_note: For 2020 model year and newer Toyota hybrid, plug-in hybrid and fuel cell vehicles: 10 years from the date the car was first used, or 150,000 miles, whichever lands first. Older ones are 8 years or 100,000 miles.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement hybrid battery pack, the single most expensive part on the car.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the car to any Toyota dealer service department with the VIN. Ask them to check the Hybrid Battery Warranty specifically, because that one runs longer than the Hybrid System Warranty that covers the other high voltage parts. If you bought the car second hand, say so anyway, because this coverage carries over to every later owner at no cost.
rules.script_hint: This is a 2020 or newer Toyota hybrid, so the hybrid battery is covered for 10 years or 150,000 miles, and that coverage transfers to me as a later owner.

rules.title: A cracked screen is never a warranty claim, but it can be $29
rules.window_note: While your AppleCare+ plan is running. The plain one year warranty never covers a drop, no matter how new the device is.
rules.what_you_get: A screen or back glass repair for a $29 fee, or other accidental damage for $99, with no cap on how many times.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether you actually have AppleCare+ under Settings, General, About, Coverage. If you do, book the repair and expect to pay the $29 service fee for screen or back glass, or $99 for other accident damage. If you do not have AppleCare+, stop here: the standard warranty covers manufacturing faults only, so a drop or a crack will be quoted at full price.
