rules.script_hint: I have AppleCare+, so this should be the $29 screen repair service fee, not a full price screen replacement.

rules.title: EU: shop finance means the lender owes you as well
rules.window_note: Only for credit that paid for that one specific purchase, such as store finance or buy-now-pay-later arranged at the till. Ordinary credit card spending does not count. You must chase the seller first and fail before you can turn to the lender. How long you have follows your own country's rules.
rules.what_you_get: If you bought something using a loan the shop arranged for that exact purchase, and the goods never arrived, only partly arrived, or are faulty, you can chase the finance company for a fix once the shop has failed to sort it out. It is the EU's version of the UK's Section 75, with the extra step that you have to try the shop first.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the shop first and keep proof they did not put it right. Then write to the finance company, explain that the credit was a linked credit agreement for that purchase, and ask them to put things right.
rules.script_hint: This was a linked credit agreement for these goods. The supplier has not given me the remedy I am entitled to, so I am pursuing my claim against you as the creditor.

rules.title: EU: free lawyers when the shop is in another country
rules.window_note: No deadline of its own, but they can only help while your underlying rights are still alive, so go early rather than late.
rules.what_you_get: The European Consumer Centres Network is a government-backed service with 29 offices across the EU, Norway and Iceland. About 150 lawyers take up your case with a shop in another country, in your own language, completely free. Useful when a foreign online seller ignores you.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to eccnet.eu, choose the centre for the country you live in, and send them your case with the receipt and the messages the shop ignored.
rules.script_hint: I bought this from a trader in another EU country, they will not honour the legal guarantee, and I would like your centre to take up my case.

rules.title: Quebec: your card issuer must reverse it, by law
rules.window_note: Cancel with the merchant first, within the deadline for your reason, for example within 30 days of the delivery date they promised. They then have 15 days to refund you. If they do not, you have 60 days after that to ask your card issuer.
rules.what_you_get: Quebec is the only place in Canada where a chargeback is a legal right instead of a favour. For anything bought online, by phone or by mail, if you cancelled properly and the merchant does not refund you within 15 days, your credit card issuer must credit your account. They must acknowledge your request within 30 days and put the money back within 90 days, or within two statement periods, whichever comes first.
rules.how_to_claim: Send your card issuer a written chargeback request naming section 54.14 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. Quebec's consumer office publishes a free template letter you can copy. Send it so you can prove it arrived, and keep a copy.
rules.script_hint: Under section 54.14 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act I am requesting that you charge back all amounts paid to this merchant and cancel all related charges on my account.

rules.title: CIBC card: warranty doubled, nothing to sign up for
rules.window_note: The extra cover starts the day the maker's warranty ends and lasts as long again, up to one extra full year. Tell them within 45 days of the loss, theft or damage, then send the completed paperwork within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: A CIBC credit card doubles the manufacturer's warranty for up to one extra full year at no cost and with no registration, on most items bought in Canada, the US or anywhere in the world when the full price went on the card. Damage or theft in the first 90 days is covered too.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-866-363-3338 free from Canada and the US, or 905-403-3338 collect, as soon as the item fails, and ask for the claim forms. Keep the store receipt, the card statement and the original manufacturer's warranty.
rules.script_hint: I am claiming under CIBC's Purchase Security and Extended Protection insurance. The manufacturer's warranty has expired and the item has failed inside the doubled term.

rules.title: Lodge replaces cracked or warped cast iron free, with no end date
rules.window_note: No deadline. It lasts as long as you own the pan, and it counts if the pan was a gift to you. It stops if you buy the pan second-hand, and it does not cover restaurant use.
rules.what_you_get: A brand new pan, free, if your bare cast iron or carbon steel cracks or warps, or came out of the factory with a hole or bad casting. Enamelled pieces are covered for chips and cracks that happen while you are cooking normally. It will not cover rust, a sticky pan, or damage from dropping it, overheating it, or putting it in the dishwasher.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to Lodge's warranty page and fill in the form for your type of pan. They will usually ask for photos of the damage first. If they want the pan back, Lodge pays the postage.
rules.script_hint: My Lodge pan cracked during normal cooking and I would like it replaced under the Made Right warranty.

rules.title: All-Clad pans, knives and bakeware carry a limited lifetime warranty
rules.window_note: No end date, but you have to be the person who bought it, you need a receipt, and it only applies in the US and Canada.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or a replacement if the metal, the construction or the workmanship was faulty. It will not cover misuse, or damage from ignoring the care instructions.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to All-Clad's warranty page, pick your product type, and send the claim in with your proof of purchase. Keep the receipt — they can refuse a claim without one.
rules.script_hint: This pan is covered by All-Clad's limited lifetime warranty and it has failed. Here is my proof of purchase.

rules.title: Zwilling knives are covered for as long as you own them
rules.window_note: It lasts for as long as you own the knife. But you must have proof you bought it — a receipt, an order email, a shop invoice, or a card or bank statement showing the purchase. No proof, no claim.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement knife or tool if yours was faulty in the metal or the making. Zwilling does not repair anything — they send you a new one, and you do not get the old one back. Normal wear from use, and blades you have blunted or damaged, are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Submit a claim through Zwilling's online Support Center with your proof of purchase. Do not take it to a Zwilling shop — shops cannot process claims. Never send in a knife you are attached to, because it will not come back.
rules.script_hint: My Zwilling knife has a fault in the material. Here is my proof of purchase — I would like a replacement under the limited warranty.

rules.title: Cutco sharpens your knives free forever, and fixes or replaces anything that stops performing
rules.window_note: Forever, and it travels with the knife. If you were given the knives, inherited them, or they were handed down, they are still covered. Home use only.
rules.what_you_get: Free sharpening whenever your knives get dull, plus a free fix or a replacement if any Cutco product stops performing properly. Sharpening itself costs nothing — you only pay return postage, which is $15 for 1 to 5 items and goes up in steps for larger batches.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in a service request on Cutco's website, print the confirmation, and post your knives with it to their service address in Olean, New York. Allow a few weeks.
rules.script_hint: These Cutco knives were passed down to me and need sharpening. The Forever Guarantee covers them even though I was not the original buyer.

rules.title: Craftsman swaps a broken hand tool for a new one, for any reason, with no receipt
rules.window_note: Forever, and no receipt is needed. Old Craftsman tools with model numbers starting with 9 get exactly the same deal as the new CMHT and CMMT ones, so tools from a parent's or grandparent's toolbox still count.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement tool. Craftsman's own wording is that if the tool fails to perform for any reason, they will replace it. This covers hammers and demolition tools, screwdrivers, pliers, hex keys, nut drivers, wrenches, ratchets and sockets, and whole mechanics tool sets.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the broken tool to a shop that stocks Craftsman and ask for a warranty swap over the counter, or ring Craftsman Customer Care and they will sort it out. Do not throw the broken tool away.
rules.script_hint: This Craftsman hand tool has the full lifetime warranty and it failed. No proof of purchase is required — I would like a replacement.

rules.title: DeWalt replaces mechanics tools that ever fail, for any reason, no receipt
rules.window_note: Forever, and no proof of purchase is needed. This is the full lifetime warranty and it covers wrenches, sockets, ratchets and drive accessories. Mechanics tools (wrenches, sockets, ratchets) have a full lifetime warranty; other hand tools have a limited lifetime warranty. Most people forget this one entirely.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement tool posted out to you. DeWalt's words are that if a DeWalt Mechanics Tool ever fails for any reason, they will replace it. Their hand tools other than mechanics tools have a narrower promise that only covers faults in the material or the making.
rules.how_to_claim: Do not take it back to the shop — DeWalt say not to. Ring DeWalt Customer Care instead and they will ship a replacement to you.
rules.script_hint: This is a DeWalt mechanics tool with the full lifetime warranty. It failed, and I understand no proof of purchase is required.

rules.title: Milwaukee hand tools carry a limited lifetime warranty, and a receipt is optional
rules.window_note: Lasts the lifetime of the tool. If you have lost the receipt it still works — Milwaukee will use the date stamped on the tool, or its serial number, to work out how old it is.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement, of a hand tool that turns out to have a fault in the material or the way it was made. It will not cover a tool you wore out, misused, or had repaired by someone else. Milwaukee power tools and batteries are different and have much shorter windows.
rules.how_to_claim: Find a Milwaukee service centre on their website and post or drop the tool off. You pay to get it there.
rules.script_hint: This Milwaukee hand tool has a limited lifetime warranty. I do not have the receipt, so please use the serial number to check the date.

rules.title: Estwing will replace an all-steel hammer that fails in normal use — but it is not a lifetime warranty
rules.window_note: There is no fixed end date on the all-steel hammers, but Estwing say in plain print on their own site that this is NOT a lifetime warranty. Their titanium hammers are only covered for 1 year, and that one cannot be passed to a new owner.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement hammer if the steel failed while you were using it the way it was meant to be used. Estwing will refuse claims for a hammer that simply wore out, got dented in the handle neck from over-striking, or was used on hardened steel like chisels or cat's paws.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty claim form on Estwing's website first — they say nothing happens until you do. Then ring them, and post the hammer with the form and a receipt from a proper retailer.
rules.script_hint: My Estwing all-steel hammer failed in normal use and I would like to make a fair claim.

rules.title: JanSport backpacks have a lifetime warranty on zips, buckles and seams
rules.window_note: Runs for the lifetime of the bag, for the first owner. It covers packs, bags, pouches, totes and cases. It does not cover JanSport clothing, hats, pins or patches, and cooler bags only get 5 years.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement, if a zip, buckle, fabric or seam failed because of how the bag was made. Normal wear, faded colour, spills and accidents are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty form on JanSport's site, or ring or email them. Then post the bag in — washed, because they charge for cleaning or send it back dirty. You pay to send it; they pay to send it home. Allow 3 to 4 weeks.
rules.script_hint: The zip on my JanSport pack has failed. I would like to claim the lifetime warranty on manufacturing defects.

rules.title: Eagle Creek's No Matter What warranty covers faults for the life of the bag
rules.window_note: It runs for the usable life of the bag — not for your lifetime. Eagle Creek are open about the difference: once wheels, handles or zips have simply worn out from years of use rather than failing from a fault, the bag has reached the end of its life and the cover stops. First owner only.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a credit toward a new bag, if a zip, wheel, handle or seam was faulty in the materials or the workmanship. Lost or stolen bags, and damage to what was inside, are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty request form on Eagle Creek's site. You pay to ship it to one of their repair centres, and they cover the parts, the labour and the trip home. Ask about a DIY repair kit first — wheels, buckles and small parts are often quicker to fix yourself.
rules.script_hint: The wheel on my Eagle Creek bag failed from a defect, not from wear. I would like to claim the No Matter What warranty.

rules.title: Tortuga covers build faults for the practical life of the bag
rules.window_note: Runs for the practical life of the bag, for the first owner. Tortuga say faults are rare and usually show up in the first few uses, so check a new bag early.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement bag or store credit if the materials, hardware or construction were faulty in a way that stops the bag working. Airline damage is not covered — claim that from the airline instead. Once the bag is genuinely worn out, Tortuga will point you to a repair partner to keep it going.
rules.how_to_claim: Email Tortuga with photos of the problem and your order number.
rules.script_hint: There is a defect in the hardware on my Tortuga bag. Photos and my order number are attached — I would like to claim the Worldwide Warranty.

rules.title: The North Face covers build faults for the working life of the item
rules.window_note: Runs for the practical, reasonably expected life of the item, not a set number of years. Footwear is not covered, and neither are second-hand items from The North Face Renewed.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement, if a seam, zip or fabric failed because of the way it was made. Accidents, poor care, normal wear and colours fading over time are not covered. Only original, unaltered items count.
rules.how_to_claim: Send the item in for warranty assessment through The North Face's warranty page. They may ask for proof of purchase, so dig out the receipt or order email if you can.
rules.script_hint: The seam on this jacket has failed from a manufacturing defect. I would like it assessed under the Limited Lifetime Warranty.

rules.title: Darn Tough replaces worn-through socks free, forever, with no receipt
rules.window_note: Forever. There is no time limit, no registration and no receipt needed — Darn Tough knit their name into every sock, so the sock itself is the proof. You can send several pairs in on one claim.
rules.what_you_get: A credit code by email for the full value of a new pair, which you spend on their site with free shipping. It covers socks that have worn through with holes, or been damaged by accident, as long as there is enough left to tell they are Darn Tough. Seconds and irregulars, and socks you have dyed or altered, are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the claim form at warranty.darntough.com, wash the socks, put the printed form in the parcel and post them back. Processing usually takes a week or two.
rules.script_hint: These Darn Tough socks have worn through. I am claiming the unconditional lifetime guarantee — no receipt is needed.

rules.title: Smartwool gives you two years to be unhappy with anything you bought
rules.window_note: Two years from the day you bought it. This one is NOT for life, so check the date on the receipt before you count on it. Items bought second-hand through thredUP, or from a seller Smartwool have not authorised, do not qualify.
rules.what_you_get: A digital gift card for the value, so you can pick something new yourself. In the US you usually do not even have to post the old item back any more.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the Smartwool Product Guarantee Form on their site and upload four photos: the whole item, a close-up of the problem, and your receipt or order confirmation. File a separate claim for each item.
rules.script_hint: I bought these within the last two years and I am not happy with how they have held up. I would like to use the Smartwool guarantee.

rules.title: Zippo fixes any windproof lighter free, however old it is
rules.window_note: For the life of the lighter, on Zippo windproof pocket lighters. Decades-old lighters still qualify and no receipt is needed. Their other products — butane lighters, hand warmers, multipurpose lighters — are handled under separate, shorter terms.
rules.what_you_get: Your lighter repaired free. Zippo's own promise is 'It works or we fix it free.' A worn-off finish or decoration is a cosmetic issue and is handled differently from a lighter that will not light.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the repair form for windproof lighters in Zippo's help centre and post the lighter to their repair clinic in Bradford, Pennsylvania.
rules.script_hint: My Zippo windproof lighter has stopped working. I am sending it in under the 'it works or we fix it free' lifetime warranty.

rules.title: Leatherman multi-tools carry a 25-year warranty
rules.window_note: 25 years from the date you bought it, for the first owner only. Leatherman Insiders members get 40 years. It is long, but it is not forever, so work out how old the tool is.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement tool if they cannot fix it. If your model has been discontinued they swap it for something of equal or greater value. Owners of MagnaCut blades also get free sharpening. Rust, scratches, sheaths, coatings and general blunting are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty form on Leatherman's site, print the packing slip, and post the tool in using a tracked, insured service. They pay to send it back. Allow about two to three weeks.
rules.script_hint: This Leatherman is inside its 25-year warranty and a tool on it has failed. I would like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: Victorinox covers Swiss Army knives and kitchen knives for their lifetime
rules.window_note: For the lifetime of the product. That covers knives, cutlery and tableware, personal care tools, sharpeners and kitchen utensils. Anything electronic (USB knives, LED lights), plus lanyards, pouches, straps, knife blocks and small leather goods, only gets 2 years.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or a replacement if there was a fault in the material or the making. If parts for your model no longer exist, they use comparable ones. Normal wear, cosmetic marks, and damage from rough handling or accidents are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to a Victorinox shop or service centre, or post it in. They may ask you to show proof of purchase, and they cover the trip back, though a handling fee can apply.
rules.script_hint: There is a manufacturing fault in my Victorinox knife. I would like it repaired under the lifetime warranty.

rules.title: Fisher Space Pen guarantees its pens for the life of the pen
rules.window_note: For the lifetime of the pen and its refill cartridges. Ink you have used up, and worn-out erasers and O-rings, are normal running costs and are not covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a new pen if they choose to replace it. Damage from dropping it, misuse, poor care, normal wear or cosmetic marks is not covered. They cannot post out loose parts like springs, so a pen needing parts has to go in.
rules.how_to_claim: Print the warranty directions from the Fisher site, put them in the parcel, and post the pen to their repairs address in Boulder City, Nevada. You pay the postage there. Allow at least three weeks, or six between November and January.
rules.script_hint: My Fisher Space Pen has a manufacturing fault. I am sending it in under the lifetime guarantee.

rules.title: Briggs & Riley repairs your bag for life, even when the airline broke it
rules.window_note: For life, and no proof of purchase is needed. This is one of the very few luggage promises that covers damage someone else caused, including baggage handlers.
rules.what_you_get: Free repair of anything that stops the bag working — wheels, handles, zips, frames — including damage done by an airline. Cosmetic scuffs, cleaning, stains and smells are not covered, and neither is a lost or stolen bag or what was inside it.
rules.how_to_claim: Submit a repair on the Briggs & Riley website, or take the bag to an authorised repair centre. You pay to send it in and they pay to send it home. Ask about a DIY repair kit first — many wheel and buckle fixes are easy at home. If an airline damaged it and you want to hold them responsible, file with the airline before you leave the airport; otherwise just send it to Briggs & Riley and they fix it free.
rules.script_hint: This bag is covered by the Simple As That lifetime guarantee. The wheel is broken and I would like it repaired free of charge.

rules.title: Herman Miller chairs get 12 years of free parts and free labour
rules.window_note: 12 years from the date you bought it, and it assumes round-the-clock use, so heavy use does not shorten it. Because it is 12 years and not forever, check the date before you assume you have run out — most people write these chairs off far too early.
rules.what_you_get: Free parts and free labour to fix a chair that failed — gas cylinders, casters, tilts, arm pads, electrics and other moving parts included. In the US and Canada the cost of the service visit is covered too.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the dealer or shop you bought it from. Before you call, take a photo of the manufacturing label underneath the chair, which has the product number, the FO number and the date it was made, plus photos of what has gone wrong. If the label is gone, your receipt can stand in.
rules.script_hint: This chair is inside its 12-year warranty and the gas cylinder has failed. I would like it repaired under warranty, parts and labour included.

rules.title: Steelcase covers a chair frame for life and its moving parts for 12 years
rules.window_note: The frame, base and structure have no end date — Steelcase say it runs for the normal expected life of the product, no matter how many shifts a day it is used. The moving parts stop at 12 years. It only counts for the first owner, so a second-hand chair is not covered. If you bought yours from a shop as an ordinary customer rather than through a dealer, Steelcase point you to a separate consumer version of the same promise.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement part, for the frame, seat shell, outer back, arm frame and base with no time limit. Tilt mechanisms, gas cylinders, arm caps, foam, casters and glides are covered for 12 years. Normal wear and tear is not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the Steelcase dealer you bought it from, or ring Steelcase directly. They may ask you to send the broken part back before they replace it.
rules.script_hint: My Steelcase chair's tilt mechanism has failed. It is under 12 years old, so I would like a replacement part under the limited lifetime warranty.

rules.title: Red Wing will resole welted boots at any age, and free-fix faults in the first year
rules.window_note: The free part is short: 12 months from purchase for Red Wing branded work boots, and you need the original receipt. The paid resole has no age limit at all, as long as the boot was built with welt construction and the uppers and insoles are still sound.
rules.what_you_get: Free repair or a new pair if a genuine fault shows up in the first 12 months of normal use. After that it is not free — but Red Wing's own repair shop will resole welted boots for around $165, or do a full package for around $180, which is far cheaper than replacing them. Boots with cracked insoles, torn uppers or worn-through linings usually cannot be saved.
rules.how_to_claim: Print the repair form from Red Wing's repairs page, then take the boots and the form to a Red Wing shop, or ring customer service and ask for the free shipping label — they cover postage on any repair over $50.
rules.script_hint: I would like my welted Red Wing boots resoled, and a free shipping label since the repair is over $50.

rules.title: Costco refunds electronics in full for 90 days
rules.window_note: 90 days from the day you got it. This covers TVs, projectors, computers, tablets, smart watches, phones, cameras, drones and big appliances like fridges, washers, dryers and dishwashers.
rules.what_you_get: All your money back. Not a repair, not a store credit - the price you actually paid.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to the returns counter at any Costco warehouse with your membership card. If you bought it online you can still bring it to a warehouse, or start the return on Costco.com.
rules.script_hint: I bought this here about two months ago and I'd like to return it under the 90-day electronics policy.

rules.title: Costco's satisfaction guarantee has no deadline on most things
rules.window_note: No time limit. A mattress, a vacuum or a jacket you bought years ago still counts. Only electronics and big appliances have the 90-day cutoff, plus a short list of things they never take back (custom orders, gift cards, tickets, precious metals, big diamonds, cigarettes and alcohol).
rules.what_you_get: All your money back, the full price you paid.
rules.how_to_claim: Bring it to the returns counter at any Costco warehouse with your membership card and say you're not satisfied with it.
rules.script_hint: I'm not satisfied with this. Costco guarantees satisfaction on everything it sells, so I'd like a refund.

rules.title: Costco doubles the maker's warranty to 2 years on TVs, computers and big appliances
rules.window_note: 2 years counted from the day you bought it in the warehouse, or the day it was delivered if you ordered online. This still works long after the 90-day return window has closed - it's the single most useful thing on this list for a TV or fridge that dies in year two.
rules.what_you_get: Your warranty runs for two years instead of one, so a fault in the second year still gets sorted out free. Covers TVs, projectors, computers (not touchscreen tablets) and major appliances - fridges over 10 cubic feet, freezers, ranges, cooktops, over-the-range microwaves, dishwashers, water heaters, washers and dryers.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Costco Technical and Warranty Service. Tell them what you bought, roughly when, and what's gone wrong. Have your membership number handy. English and Spanish agents, calls answered in the US.
rules.script_hint: I bought this at Costco about fourteen months ago and it's stopped working. Costco extends the manufacturer's warranty to two years - can you help me get it fixed?

rules.title: L.L.Bean refunds anything for a year, no reason needed
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. You don't have to prove anything is broken - not being happy with it is enough.
rules.what_you_get: All your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Mail it back or take it to an L.L.Bean store. You do need proof you bought it: a receipt, the order email, or your order history if you were signed in when you bought it.
rules.script_hint: I'm not 100 percent satisfied with this and it's less than a year old, so I'd like a refund under your guarantee.

rules.title: L.L.Bean still looks at older gear that fell apart on its own
rules.window_note: No deadline, but this only covers things that were badly made - a seam that let go, a zip that was faulty from the start. It does not cover gear you simply wore out.
rules.what_you_get: They look at it and decide. If it really is a fault in the material or the stitching, you can get a refund. This one is not automatic - it's a judgement call on their side.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact L.L.Bean, say clearly that the item failed because of how it was made rather than from normal use, and send photos of the fault.
rules.script_hint: This seam came apart on its own - that's a craftsmanship fault, not wear and tear. Your guarantee says you'll still consider items like this after a year.

rules.title: REI takes outdoor electronics back for 90 days
rules.window_note: 90 days for everyone, member or not. This is the one thing the one-year member window does not stretch. Covers activity trackers, GPS devices, bike trainers, emergency communication devices and cameras.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement or all your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any REI store or start the return online, and mention it's an outdoor electronics item so they use the right window.
rules.script_hint: This GPS unit is inside the 90-day outdoor electronics window and it isn't working right - I'd like a refund or a replacement.

rules.title: MEC's guarantee covers being sold the wrong thing, not just broken things
rules.window_note: No deadline. Most people never claim this one because they assume a guarantee only covers faults - MEC's also covers the advice a staff member gave you.
rules.what_you_get: Money back or store credit even though nothing is broken, because the gear you were pointed at was wrong for you.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it back to MEC and explain that staff recommended this for what you were doing and it turned out to be the wrong choice.
rules.script_hint: I was advised this was right for what I needed and it isn't. Your Rocksolid Guarantee covers product selection advice, so I'd like a refund or credit.

rules.title: John Lewis puts a free 5-year guarantee on every TV
rules.window_note: 5 years from when you bought it, on every TV they sell, at no extra cost. Most TV makers only give you one or two years, so years three to five are pure John Lewis.
rules.what_you_get: A repair or a replacement TV, and you pay nothing for it.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact John Lewis customer services with your order number. Tell them the TV is faulty and that it came with their free 5-year guarantee.
rules.script_hint: This TV came with John Lewis's free 5-year guarantee and it's developed a fault - I'd like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: Amazon refunds you itself when a third-party seller won't
rules.window_note: You have 90 days from the last delivery date on the order. Message the seller first and give them 48 hours - if you skip that step Amazon will bounce the claim. To get a refund on a return you also need to ask for the return within 30 days of delivery.
rules.what_you_get: Amazon pays you back out of its own pocket when the seller ignores you or refuses. Covers items that turn up damaged, faulty, or not what the listing said.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to Your Orders, message the seller and describe the problem. Wait 48 hours. If they haven't fixed it, go back to that order and choose Problem with order, then file an A-to-z Guarantee claim.
rules.script_hint: The item arrived faulty and the seller hasn't resolved it more than 48 hours after I contacted them, so I'm filing an A-to-z Guarantee claim.

rules.title: Zappos pays the postage on returns for 60 days
rules.window_note: 60 days from when you bought it. What counts is the day the courier scans your package, not the day it gets back to them - so dropping it off on day 59 is fine. Heads up: older guides say Zappos gives you 365 days. That's out of date - their current policy is 60.
rules.what_you_get: All your money back, and you don't pay a penny to ship it back, anywhere in the US including military addresses.
rules.how_to_claim: Start the return on Zappos.com, print the free label and drop the parcel off. Shoes have to go back in their original box, still in good shape, and the item has to be unworn with tags on.
rules.script_hint: I'm returning this inside the 60-day window - I'd like the free return label.

rules.title: Decathlon warranties its own-brand gear and pays the return postage
rules.window_note: Decathlon sets a different length for every product and prints it on that product's own page on their website. Look yours up before you give up - don't assume it has run out. Their plain 30-day return window is separate and much shorter.
rules.what_you_get: A repair or a replacement if the thing was badly made. You pay to send it in, but Decathlon pays to send it back to you.
rules.how_to_claim: Email Decathlon customer service with your receipt, the date you bought it, and photos or a short video of the fault. Keep the receipt - without it they won't process the claim.
rules.script_hint: This Decathlon-branded item has a fault in the material, not wear and tear. I'd like to claim under your limited warranty - my receipt and photos are attached.

rules.title: LG washer: 10 years on the motor, forever on the drum
rules.window_note: The whole washer is covered for 1 year. The drum motor is covered for 10 years. The stainless steel drum has no end date at all - it is covered for as long as you own the machine.
rules.what_you_get: If the motor in your LG washer dies, LG gives you a new one free for up to 10 years. If the stainless steel drum cracks or fails, LG gives you a new drum free with no time limit. You pay the repair person; LG pays for the part.
rules.how_to_claim: Call LG at 1-800-243-0000 with your model number, serial number and receipt. Say the drum motor or the stainless drum has failed and you want the part under warranty.
rules.script_hint: My LG washer's drum motor has failed. LG's warranty covers the drum motor - stator, rotor and hall sensor - for ten years, and the stainless steel drum for the lifetime of the machine. Please send the part under warranty.

rules.title: LG dishwasher: 10 years on the motor, forever on the tub
rules.window_note: Everything is covered for 1 year with free repair work, then parts only: 2 years on most parts, 5 years on the control board and the racks, 10 years on the Direct Drive motor, and no time limit on the stainless steel tub and door liner while you still own it.
rules.what_you_get: Free replacement parts long after most people think the warranty ran out. A dead motor gets a free motor for 10 years. A rack that falls apart gets a free rack for 5 years. A leaking or cracked stainless tub or door liner gets a free replacement with no end date.
rules.how_to_claim: Call LG at 1-800-243-0000 with your model number, serial number and receipt, and name the exact part that failed.
rules.script_hint: My LG dishwasher's [motor / rack / stainless tub] has failed. LG covers the Direct Drive motor for ten years, the rack and control board for five, and the stainless tub and door liner for the lifetime of the machine. I'd like that part under warranty.

rules.title: Samsung: free extra year of warranty on 2026 summer purchases
rules.window_note: Only for eligible Samsung appliances bought between 9 July 2026 and 30 September 2026. You have to send in the claim form yourself - Samsung's page says within 30 days after the offer ends.
rules.what_you_get: One extra free year of warranty on top of the normal one, so two years of parts and labour instead of one. It is free, but only if you claim it.
rules.how_to_claim: Open the Samsung SmartThings app, find the offer claim form, and submit it with your receipt. Do it as soon as you buy - do not wait, because the claim window closes shortly after 30 September 2026.
rules.script_hint: I bought this Samsung appliance during the free two-year warranty offer and I'm submitting my claim form through SmartThings to register the extra year.

rules.title: Maytag washer: 10 years on the motor and the wash basket
rules.window_note: Year 1 covers everything including the repair work. Years 2 to 10 cover two parts only - the wash basket drive motor and the side walls of the stainless steel wash basket - and you pay the repair person.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement drive motor or stainless wash basket up to 10 years after you bought the washer. That is usually the most expensive part of the machine.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Maytag customer service (the number is in your use and care guide) or book through maytag.com, give your model and serial number and the original purchase date, and ask for the 10-year drive motor and wash basket parts warranty.
rules.script_hint: My Maytag washer's drive motor has failed. Maytag's limited warranty covers the wash basket drive motor and the stainless steel wash basket side walls from the second through the tenth year. I'd like the part supplied under that warranty.

rules.title: KitchenAid dishwasher: the stainless tub is covered forever
rules.window_note: 1 year on everything. Years 2 to 5 cover the nylon racks and the electronic controls (parts only). The stainless steel tub and inner door liner are covered for the life of the dishwasher - and that one includes the repair work too.
rules.what_you_get: If the stainless steel tub or inner door liner of your KitchenAid dishwasher fails, KitchenAid pays for both the part and the repair, with no time limit. Racks that fall apart and dead control boards are free parts for 5 years.
rules.how_to_claim: Call KitchenAid at 1-800-422-1230 with your model and serial number and proof of the purchase date, and name the part that failed.
rules.script_hint: My KitchenAid dishwasher's stainless steel tub has failed. KitchenAid gives a lifetime limited warranty on the stainless steel tub and inner door liner, covering parts and repair labour. Please book service under that warranty.

rules.title: Bosch dishwasher: rust through the tub means a new dishwasher
rules.window_note: 365 days on everything. Then 5 years on the circuit board and 5 years on the dish racks (parts only). If the stainless steel inside rusts right through, there is no time limit at all.
rules.what_you_get: If the inner liner of your Bosch dishwasher rusts through, Bosch repairs it or gives you the same model or a better current one - no matter how old it is. They do the same for a stainless door that rusts through. Broken racks and dead circuit boards are free parts for 5 years.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Bosch at 1-800-944-2904 with your model and serial number (on the edge of the door) and say the inner liner has rusted through, or that a rack or the circuit board has failed.
rules.script_hint: The inner liner of my Bosch dishwasher has rusted through. Bosch's lifetime warranty against stainless steel rust-through says you repair or replace the dishwasher. Please open a claim.

rules.title: Bosch: the warranty stays with the appliance, not the buyer
rules.window_note: Applies for whatever is left of the warranty term. Useful if you bought a house with Bosch appliances already in it, or bought one second hand.
rules.what_you_get: You can still claim on a Bosch warranty even if you were not the person who bought the appliance. Bosch's warranty says it applies to the original buyer and to every later owner. You also do not have to have registered it - Bosch says registration is not needed for cover.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Bosch at 1-800-944-2904 with the model and serial number. If they ask for the original receipt and you do not have one, tell them you are a later owner and ask them to use the manufacture date or the home's closing date.
rules.script_hint: I'm not the original buyer of this Bosch appliance - it came with the house. Bosch's warranty says it applies to each succeeding owner during the term, and that registration isn't necessary for coverage. Please book warranty service.

rules.title: Miele fridge and wine cooler: 10 years on the cooling parts
rules.window_note: The cooling system is covered for 5 years with the repair work included, then for another 5 years for the part only. That is 10 years in total from the purchase date.
rules.what_you_get: If your Miele fridge, freezer or wine cooler stops cooling, the compressor, condenser, evaporator, drier, refrigerant and tubing are fixed free for 5 years, and the parts are still free in years 6 to 10.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Miele USA through mieleusa.com or your authorised Miele dealer, give the model and serial number and the purchase date, and say it is a sealed refrigeration system fault.
rules.script_hint: My Miele wine cooler has stopped cooling. Miele's warranty covers the sealed refrigeration system for five years parts and labour and a further five years for parts. Please book service under that warranty.

rules.title: Miele: 2 years, not 1, on home appliances
rules.window_note: Two full years from the purchase date, for ovens, hobs, hoods, coffee machines, fridges, dishwashers, washing machines and dryers used at home.
rules.what_you_get: Free repair, parts and labour, for two years - double the one year most brands give. Buy from an authorised Miele dealer and keep the receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Miele USA through mieleusa.com or the dealer you bought from, with your model and serial number and the receipt. Say it is still inside the two-year warranty.
rules.script_hint: My Miele [dishwasher] has failed and it's under two years old. Miele's limited warranty for residential appliances is two years covering parts and labour, so I'd like a warranty repair booked.

rules.title: Frigidaire and Electrolux fridge: 5 years on the cooling parts
rules.window_note: 1 year on everything including the repair work. Years 2 to 5 cover the cooling parts only - the compressor, condenser, evaporator and tubing - and you pay the call-out and the labour.
rules.what_you_get: A free compressor or other cooling part up to 5 years after you bought the fridge or freezer. The compressor is normally the single most expensive thing in the machine.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-944-9044 with the model and serial number and the purchase date, and say it is a sealed refrigeration system failure.
rules.script_hint: My Frigidaire refrigerator has stopped cooling. Your limited warranty covers the sealed refrigeration system - compressor, condenser, evaporator and tubing - from the second through the fifth year. Please supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Speed Queen washer and dryer: 3 to 7 years, parts and labour
rules.window_note: How long depends on the model: TR3 and DR3 get 3 years, TR5, DR5, TC5, DC5, FF7, DF7 and SF7 get 5 years, and TR7 and DR7 rear-control models get 7 years. Counted from the day it was installed. The cover also passes to a new owner if you sell the machine. Watch out: if you never registered it within the first year, cover starts 30 days after it left the factory, not when you bought it.

TWO GOTCHAS WORTH SURFACING IN THE UI:

REGIONS: almost everything here is scoped to US because I read the US-specific warranty documents. Several of these brands offer similar or better terms in the EU/UK, where statutory rights add a separate two-year layer — that belongs in a statutory-rules batch, not this one.

COVERAGE AND SOURCING

Every rule above was read from a primary or issuer-published benefit document, not from a blog summary. Sources used: Visa's own terms PDFs on usa.visa.com (purchase security and extended warranty, effective 4/15/21); the American Express US Extended Warranty, Purchase Protection and Return Protection benefit guides on americanexpress.com (rev. 4/19/2024, 10/2020 editions); Amex Bank of Canada's Certificate of Insurance (amended and restated effective 1 July 2025); Mastercard Guide to Benefits booklets published by a credit union (core credit) and by Capital One (World Elite); Chase's own education pages; Canadian Tire's Triangle World Elite certificate booklet; Scotiabank's Visa Infinite purchase security certificate.

THE BIG HONEST CAVEAT: WHETHER A GIVEN CARD HAS THE BENEFIT AT ALL

Visa and Mastercard set the standard terms, but each bank decides whether to include them. So a rule marked "likely" means the terms are verified but you cannot promise that any particular Visa or Mastercard carries the benefit. The product should tell users to look up their own card's Guide to Benefits rather than assert coverage. Amex is the exception: Amex is both issuer and network, so its terms are marked "certain", though Amex still says only "eligible cards" qualify (return protection in particular sits on fewer cards, which is why it is marked "likely").

CARDS THAT DROPPED THESE BENEFITS (verified, useful as negative answers)
- Discover: ended extended warranty, purchase protection and return guarantee on 28 February 2018. Discover is the one major US network with none of these. Answer for Discover users should be "your card does not cover this, but the manufacturer or a state law might".
- Citi: cut extended warranty, damage and theft purchase protection, 90-day return protection and Price Rewind on 22 September 2019, then added a 24-month extended warranty back to some cards (Double Cash, Custom Cash) from 17 November 2024. Citi also removed extended warranty from the Costco card around early 2023. Citi is the messiest issuer to reason about.
- Capital One QuickSilver Mastercard: lost extended warranty and price protection from 1 September 2021 (reporting suggested the Visa version may have been unaffected — unverified).
- Chase dropped price protection and return protection across all cards in 2018 but kept purchase protection and extended warranty.
- Amex halved its extended warranty from 2 extra years to 1 extra year for purchases made from 1 October 2020.
- Price protection is effectively dead everywhere: Visa and Mastercard ended their network programs in 2018. Do not build price-drop refunds into the product.

DETAILS I COULD NOT PIN DOWN
- The Visa benefit administrator phone number differs by issuer. Visa's own current PDFs use 1-888-221-3289 and cardbenefitservices.com; some issuer guides (e.g. UBS, Bank of America) still print 1-800-397-9010. The safest instruction is "call the number on the back of your card". I used Visa's own number and said so.
- Mastercard purchase assurance caps vary a lot by card ($1,000 per loss on the Capital One World Elite guide I read; other issuers differ). I stated the number I verified and flagged that it varies.
- I did not verify a live Citi Guide to Protection Benefits PDF: the cardbenefits.citi.com link I tried returned "item not found", so the Citi numbers come from a mirrored copy of Citi's May 2024 guide. Citi's claim reporting wording in that document is "as soon as possible after the Incident" with documents due within 180 days — I did not find a hard day count for first notice, so I did not invent one. Citi is marked "likely" and its source_url points at Citi's live benefits site rather than the mirror.
- I could not read the Visa Signature PDF directly (encoding failure), so the Signature terms were confirmed through an issuer-hosted copy of the same Visa language and are described together with Infinite, whose Visa-hosted PDF I did read in full. The two are identical on every number I checked.
- Amex US purchase protection and extended warranty both require Notice of Claim "within thirty (30) days of the loss or as soon as reasonably possible". The 30-day figure is explicit in the extended warranty guide and on Amex's own credit-intel page; in the purchase protection PDF that clause was garbled by text extraction, so I carried the same 30 days across but flag it here.
- Canadian terms vary by issuer more than US ones. Purchase security notice deadlines I found range from 30 days (RBC's Visa Infinite wording, seen only in search results) to 45 days (Scotiabank, read in full) to 90 days (Triangle Mastercard, read in full). Amex Canada's 48-hour reporting rule is real and read directly from the July 2025 certificate — it is the single most missable deadline in this whole set and is worth surfacing loudly.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT
- Price protection and Citi Price Rewind: discontinued.
- Wells Fargo: widely reported to have no extended warranty on any card, but I did not find a Wells Fargo primary document saying so, so I made no rule and no claim.
- Cell phone protection: a real and valuable card benefit, but it is a separate product from the three you asked about and usually requires paying the phone bill with the card.
- Category lists are my judgement about what these benefits normally cover, not quoted from the documents. Every one of these benefits excludes motor vehicles, software, consumables, live plants and animals, used or refurbished goods, and anything bought for business resale. E-bikes and motorised scooters are explicitly excluded in the Amex Canada certificate, so "bike" is omitted there.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANGLE
Extended warranty is the strongest fit for the landfill story: it pays for a repair on an item the maker has stopped standing behind, and the documents literally require a repair estimate from an authorised shop before they will replace anything. Purchase protection is more often a payout than a repair.

15 rules, all statutory (consumer law that beats the printed warranty). Verification method and honest caveats:

WHAT I VERIFIED AGAINST PRIMARY SOURCES (fetched and read the actual text):
- 15 U.S.C. 2302(c), 2308, 2310(d) and 16 CFR 700.10 via Cornell LII — the anti-tying rule, the disclaimer ban, and the attorney-fee provision are quoted from statute.
- UK Consumer Rights Act 2015 Part 1 Ch. 2 via legislation.gov.uk — 30-day right to reject (s.22), satisfactory quality incl. durability (s.9), six-month presumption (s.19(14)).
- California Civil Code 1791.1(c), 1793.2(d) and 1793.03 via leginfo.legislature.ca.gov — the 60-day/1-year implied warranty, the replace-or-refund duty, and the 3-year/7-year parts rule.
- BC Sale of Goods Act ss.18(c) and 20(2) via bclaws.gov.bc.ca — the durability condition and the void-waiver rule.
- Colorado HB24-1121 via leg.colorado.gov — the 1 Jan 2026 date and the parts-pairing ban wording.
- Minnesota Stat. 325E.72 via revisor.mn.gov — the "fair and reasonable terms" duty and the ban on requiring pairing/registration.
- EU legal guarantee via europa.eu Your Europe (official EU citizen portal) — 2 years minimum, 1-year reversed burden of proof, claim lies against the seller.
- Quebec legal warranty via Éducaloi — arts. 37/38, claimable against merchant OR manufacturer, free, survives the printed warranty.
- OPC phone (1 888 672-2556) and Citizens Advice consumer helpline (0808 223 1133) both verified on their own sites. FTC reporting URL verified.

WHERE I HAD TO RELY ON SECONDARY SOURCES:
- EUR-Lex and ftc.gov both blocked full-text fetching (403 / empty extraction). For the EU Right to Repair Directive 2024/1799 I cross-checked three independent sources (Right to Repair Europe, Freshfields on the German implementing bill, EUR-Lex's own summary page) and they agree on: producer duty to repair Annex II goods at a reasonable price outside the guarantee, the one-off 12-month extension when you choose repair over replacement, and the 31 July 2026 transposition deadline. For the FTC material I relied on FTC-domain search results describing their own pages plus the underlying statute, which I did read.
- Quebec's warranty of good working order durations come from Osler's summary of the published regulation, not the regulation text itself. Marked certain because the durations were consistent across Osler, Stikeman and McCarthy, but the source_url is a law firm page rather than a statute.
- EU ecodesign 2023/1670 specifics (7 years, 5-10 working days, 800 cycles, 5 years of OS updates, 15 parts to repairers) come from consistent secondary reporting; the EUR-Lex text itself would not extract. source_url points at the European Commission's own product page.

DELIBERATE HONESTY CHOICES:
- I left `contact` empty on five rules rather than guess at an Attorney General complaint URL or a company line I had not confirmed.
- `us-implied-warranty-merchantability` is marked "likely" only because the four-year window is UCC 2-725 as adopted by most states — a handful differ, and I did not audit all 50.
- `ca-durability-implied-warranty` is marked "likely" because I verified BC's wording directly but generalised "most provinces have a similar rule" without checking each one; the roughly-two-year court deadline is a general statement, not a per-province check.
- `eu-right-to-repair-directive` is marked "likely" because Right to Repair Europe explicitly stated that as of the 31 July 2026 deadline several member states had not finished transposing, so a given user's country may not have it live yet.
- Quebec's warranty of good working order does not start until 5 October 2026 (about six weeks after today). I included it because it is fully enacted with published durations, but the window_note says plainly when it starts. I did not verify whether it reaches goods bought before that date, so I avoided claiming either way.

GAPS I DID NOT FILL:
- No `deadline` values are set — none of these are settlements, so none have claim deadlines.
- Washington state's electronics repair law appeared in search results but I could not confirm its effective date, so I left it out entirely rather than name it.
- Saskatchewan and New Brunswick let consumers claim directly against manufacturers, which is unusually strong, but it is single-province coverage and I did not verify it to primary-source level, so it is not included.
- I did not name which specific five spare parts must go to end-users under the EU phone rules, because I could only confirm the count, not the list.
